body.text: sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya vikalpāj jātibahutvam iti saṃkṣepeṇoktaṃ, tad vistareṇa vibhajyate -- tāḥ khalv imā jātayaḥ sthāpanāhetau prayukte caturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣedhahetavaḥ /
body.translated_text: It has been said in brief that there are many kinds of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders) due to the variety of objections based on similarity and dissimilarity. Now that is being explained in detail — These futile rejoinders are indeed twenty-four refutation-reasons employed when a probative reason is adduced:

children.text: sādharmya-vaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya vikalpāj jātibahutvam iti saṃkṣepeṇa uktaṃ, tad vistareṇa vibhajyate --- tāḥ khalv imā jātayaḥ sthāpanā-hetau prayukte caturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣedhahetavaḥ /

body.text: sādharmyavaidharmyotkarṣāpakarṣavarṇyāvarṇyavikalpasādhyaprāptyaprāptiprasaṅgapratidṛṣṭāntānutpattisaṃśayaprakaraṇāhetvarthāpattyaviśeṣopapattyupalabdhyanupalabdhyanityanityakāryasamāḥ //
body.translated_text: The [futile rejoinders] based on similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>), superiority (<s>utkarṣa</s>), inferiority (<s>apakarṣa</s>), the explainable (<s>varṇya</s>), the inexplainable (<s>avarṇya</s>), alternative (<s>vikalpa</s>), what-is-to-be-proved (<s>sādhya</s>), attainment (<s>prāpti</s>), non-attainment (<s>aprāpti</s>), implication (<s>prasaṅga</s>), counter-example (<s>pratidṛṣṭānta</s>), non-origination (<s>anutpatti</s>), doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), topic (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), non-reason (<s>ahetu</s>), presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), non-distinction (<s>aviśeṣa</s>), cogency (<s>upapatti</s>), perception (<s>upalabdhi</s>), non-perception (<s>anupalabdhi</s>), impermanence (<s>anitya</s>), permanence (<s>nitya</s>), and effect (<s>kārya</s>) — these are the 'equal' rejoinders.

children.text: sādharmya-vaidharmya-utkarṣa-apakarṣa-varṇya-avarṇya-vikalpa-sādhya-prāpty-aprāpti-prasaṅga-pratidṛṣṭānta-anutpatti-saṃśaya-prakaraṇa-ahetv-arthāpatty-aviśeṣa-upapatty-upalabdhy-anupalabdhy-anitya-nitya-kāryasamāḥ //

body.text: jāteḥ saṃkṣepeṇoktāyā vistaro vaktavya itīdānīm ārabhyate sādharmyādisūtram -- sādharmyavaidharmyotkarṣāpakarṣavarṇyāvarṇyavikalpasādhyaprāptyaprāptiprasaṅgapratidṛṣṭāntānutpattisaṃśayaprakaraṇāhetvarthāpattyaviśeṣopapattyupalabdhyanupalabdhyanityanityakāryasamāḥ / sādharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ sthāpanāhetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ / aviśeṣaṃ tatra tatrodāhariṣyāmaḥ / evaṃ vaidharmyasamaprabhṛtayo 'pi nirvaktavyāḥ // NySBh_20//
body.translated_text: Since the <s>jāti</s> has been stated in brief, its detailed exposition is now commenced with the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with <s>sādharmya</s> — [The rejoinders] based on similarity, dissimilarity, superiority, inferiority, the explainable, the inexplainable, alternative, what-is-to-be-proved, attainment, non-attainment, implication, counter-example, non-origination, doubt, topic, non-reason, presumption, non-distinction, cogency, perception, non-perception, impermanence, permanence, and effect are the 'equal' rejoinders. An objection based on similarity that is indistinguishable from the probative reason is the <s>sādharmya-sama</s> (similarity-equal). We shall illustrate the non-distinction in each case. Similarly, the <s>vaidharmya-sama</s> and the rest are to be explained. // NySBh_20 //

children.text: jāteḥ saṃkṣepeṇa uktāyā vistaro vaktavya iti idānīm ārabhyate sādharmya-ādi-sūtram --- sādharmya-vaidharmya-utkarṣa-apakarṣa-varṇya-avarṇya-vikalpa-sādhya-prāpty-aprāpti-prasaṅga-pratidṛṣṭānta-anutpatti-saṃśaya-prakaraṇa-ahetv-arthāpatty-aviśeṣa-upapatty-upalabdhy-anupalabdhy-anitya-nitya-kāryasamāḥ / sādharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ sthāpanā-hetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ / aviśeṣaṃ tatra tatra udāhariṣyāmaḥ / evaṃ vaidharmyasama-prabhṛtayo 'pi nirvaktavyāḥ // NySBh_20//

body.text: sādharmyavaidharmyābhyām upasaṃhāre taddharmaviparyayopapatteḥ sādharmyavaidharmyasamau //
body.translated_text: When there is a positive or negative correlation based on similarity and dissimilarity, the <s>sādharmya-sama</s> and <s>vaidharmya-sama</s> arise because the property of the subject and its contrary are both tenable.

children.text: sādharmya-vaidharmyābhyām upasaṃhāre tad-dharma-viparyaya-upapatteḥ sādharmya-vaidharmyasamau //

body.text: sādharmyeṇopasaṃhāre sādhyadharmaviparyayopapatteḥ sādharmyeṇaiva pratyavasthānam aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ sthāpanāhetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / nidarśanaṃ kriyāvān ātmā dravyasya kriyāhetuguṇayogāt / dravyaṃ loṣṭaḥ kriyāhetuguṇayuktaḥ kriyāvāṃs tathā cātmā tasmāt kriyāvān iti / evam upasaṃhṛte paraḥ sādharmyeṇaiva pratyavatiṣṭhate niṣkriya ātmā vibhuno dravyasya niṣkriyatvād vibhu cākāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ ca tathā cātmā tasmān niṣkriya iti / na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyaṃ na punar akriyasādharmyād niṣkriyeṇeti / viśeṣahetvabhāvāt sādharmyasamaḥ pratiṣedho bhavati / atha vaidharmyasamaḥ kriyāhetuguṇayukto loṣṭaḥ paricchinno dṛṣṭo na ca tathātmā tasmān na loṣṭavat kriyāvān iti / na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyaṃ na punaḥ kriyāvadvaidharmyād akriyeṇeti viśeṣahetvabhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ / vaidharmyeṇa copasaṃhāraḥ niṣkriya ātmā vibhutvāt kriyāvad dravyam avibhu dṛṣṭaṃ niṣkriyaṃ loṣṭaḥ na ca tathātmā tasmān niṣkriya iti / vaidharmyeṇa pratyavasthānaṃ niṣkriyaṃ dravyam ākāśaṃ kriyāhetuguṇarahitaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na ca tathātmā tasmān na niṣkriya iti / na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvadvaidharmyān niṣkriyeṇa bhavitavyaṃ na punar akriyavaidharmyāt kriyāvateti viśeṣahetvabhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ / atha sādharmyasamaḥ kriyāvāṃl loṣṭaḥ kriyāhetuguṇayukto dṛṣṭaḥ tathā cātmā tasmāt kriyāvān iti na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ kriyāvadvaidharmyān niṣkriyo na punaḥ kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvān iti viśeṣahetvabhāvāt sādharmyasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: When a positive correlation based on similarity is made, an objection based on the very same similarity that is indistinguishable from the probative reason is the <s>sādharmya-sama</s> (similarity-equal) refutation. For example: 'The <s>ātman</s> (self) possesses action, because of its conjunction with a substance possessing action-cause-quality.' The substance is a clod of earth; it possesses action-cause-quality and is observed to have action; so too the <s>ātman</s>, therefore it has action. When this positive correlation is made, the opponent objects based on similarity itself: 'The <s>ātman</s> is without action, because a substance that is all-pervading is observed to be without action; space is all-pervading and without action; so too the <s>ātman</s>, therefore it is without action.' There is no distinguishing reason to say that because of similarity with what has action one must have action, but not that because of similarity with what lacks action one must be without action. Due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, this is a <s>sādharmya-sama</s> refutation. Now the <s>vaidharmya-sama</s>: 'A clod, which possesses action-cause-quality, is observed to be limited; the <s>ātman</s> is not like that, therefore it does not have action like a clod.' There is no distinguishing reason to say that because of similarity with what has action one must have action, rather than that because of dissimilarity from what has action one must be without action — due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, this is a <s>vaidharmya-sama</s>. And when there is a negative correlation: 'The <s>ātman</s> is without action because it is all-pervading; an active substance is observed to be non-pervading; a clod is without action and the <s>ātman</s> is not like that, therefore it is without action.' The objection by dissimilarity: 'Space, a substance without action, is observed to lack action-cause-quality; the <s>ātman</s> is not like that, therefore it is not without action.' There is no distinguishing reason to say that because of dissimilarity from what has action one must be without action, rather than that because of dissimilarity from what lacks action one must have action — due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, this is a <s>vaidharmya-sama</s>. And the <s>sādharmya-sama</s>: 'A clod is active and observed to possess action-cause-quality; so too the <s>ātman</s>, therefore it has action.' There is no distinguishing reason — due to the absence of a distinguishing reason, this is a <s>sādharmya-sama</s>.

children.text: sādharmyeṇa upasaṃhāre sādhyadharmaviparyaya-upapatteḥ sādharmyeṇa eva pratyavasthānam aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ sthāpanā-hetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / nidarśanaṃ kriyāvān ātmā dravyasya kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yogāt / dravyaṃ loṣṭaḥ kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yuktaḥ kriyāvāṃs tathā cā atmā tasmāt kriyāvān iti / evam upasaṃhṛte paraḥ sādharmyeṇa eva pratyavatiṣṭhate niṣkriya ātmā vibhuno dravyasya niṣkriyatvād vibhu cā akāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ ca tathā cā atmā tasmān niṣkriya iti / na ca asti viśeṣa-hetuḥ kriyāvat-sādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyaṃ na punar akriyasādharmyād niṣkriyeṇa iti / viśeṣa-hetv-abhāvāt sādharmyasamaḥ pratiṣedho bhavati / atha vaidharmyasamaḥ kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yukto loṣṭaḥ paricchinno dṛṣṭo na ca tathā ātmā tasmān na loṣṭavat kriyāvān iti / na ca asti viśeṣa-hetuḥ kriyāvat-sādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyaṃ na punaḥ kriyāvad-vaidharmyād akriyeṇa iti viśeṣa-hetv-abhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ / vaidharmyeṇa ca upasaṃhāraḥ niṣkriya ātmā vibhutvāt kriyāvad dravyam avibhu dṛṣṭaṃ niṣkriyaṃ loṣṭaḥ na ca tathā ātmā tasmān niṣkriya iti / vaidharmyeṇa pratyavasthānaṃ niṣkriyaṃ dravyam ākāśaṃ kriyā-hetu-guṇa-rahitaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na ca tathā ātmā tasmān na niṣkriya iti / na ca asti viśeṣa-hetuḥ kriyāvad-vaidharmyān niṣkriyeṇa bhavitavyaṃ na punar akriyavaidharmyāt kriyāvata īti viśeṣa-hetv-abhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ / atha sādharmyasamaḥ kriyāvāṃl loṣṭaḥ kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yukto dṛṣṭaḥ tathā cā atmā tasmāt kriyāvān iti na ca asti viśeṣa-hetuḥ kriyāvad-vaidharmyān niṣkriyo na punaḥ kriyāvat-sādharmyāt kriyāvān iti viśeṣa-hetv-abhāvāt sādharmyasamaḥ //

body.text: gotvād gosiddhivat tatsiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as a cow is established through cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>), so is that [property] established through [its universal].

children.text: gotvād go-siddhivat tat-siddhiḥ //

body.text: sādharmyamātreṇa vaidharmyamātreṇa ca sādhyasādhane pratijñāyamāne syād avyavasthā sā tu dharmaviśeṣe nopapadyate gosādharmyād gotvāj jātiviśeṣād gauḥ sidhyati na tu sāsnādisambandhāt / aśvādivaidharmyād gotvād eva gauḥ sidhyati na guṇādibhedāt / tac caitat kṛtavyākhyānam avayavaprakaraṇe pramāṇānām abhisambandhāc caikārthakāritvaṃ samānaṃ vākye iti / hetvābhāsāśrayā khalv iyam avyavastheti //
body.translated_text: When the proving of the thesis is claimed merely through similarity or merely through dissimilarity, there would be indeterminacy; but that does not apply when there is a specific property. Through similarity with a cow and through cow-ness — a specific universal — a cow is established, not merely through connection with dewlap and the like. Through dissimilarity from horses and the like, a cow is established through cow-ness alone, not through difference in qualities and the like. This has already been explained in the section on the members [of a syllogism]: because of the connection with the means of valid cognition, the unity of purpose within a sentence is the same. This indeterminacy is indeed based on fallacious reasons.

children.text: sādharmya-mātreṇa vaidharmya-mātreṇa ca sādhya-sādhane pratijñāyamāne syād avyavasthā sā tu dharma-viśeṣe na upapadyate go-sādharmyād gotvāj jāti-viśeṣād gauḥ sidhyati na tu sāsnā-ādi-sambandhāt / aśva-ādi-vaidharmyād gotvād eva gauḥ sidhyati na guṇa-ādi-bhedāt / tac ca etat kṛta-vyākhyānam avayava-prakaraṇe pramāṇānām abhisambandhāc ca eka-artha-kāritvaṃ samānaṃ vākye iti / hetv-ābhāsāśrayā khalv iyam avyavastha īti //

body.text: sādhyadṛṣṭāntayor dharmavikalpād ubhayasādhyatvāc cotkarśāpakarśavarṇyāvarṇyavikalpasādhyasamāḥ //
body.translated_text: Due to the differentiation of properties between the thesis and the example, and because both require proof, the [rejoinders] based on superiority, inferiority, the explainable, the inexplainable, alternative, and what-is-to-be-proved are <s>utkarṣa-apakarṣa-varṇya-avarṇya-vikalpa-sādhya-samāḥ</s>.

children.text: sādhya-dṛṣṭāntayor dharma-vikalpād ubhaya-sādhyatvāc ca utkarśa-apakarśa-varṇya-avarṇya-vikalpa-sādhyasamāḥ //

body.text: dṛṣṭāntadharmaṃ sādhye samāsañjayata utkarśasamaḥ / yadi kriyāhetuguṇayogāl loṣṭavat kriyāvān ātmā loṣṭavad eva sparśavān api prāpnoti / atha na sparśavāṃl loṣṭavat kriyāvān api na prāpnoti viparyaye vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti / sādhye dharmābhāvaṃ dṛṣṭāntāt prasañjayato 'pakarśasamaḥ / loṣṭaḥ khalu kriyāvān avibhur dṛṣṭaḥ kāmam ātmāpi kriyāvān avibhur astu viparyaye vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti / khyāpanīyo varṇyo viparyayād avarṇyaḥ tāv etau sādhyadṛṣṭāntadharmau viparyasyato varṇyāvarṇyasamau bhavataḥ / sādhanadharmayukte dṛṣṭānte dharmāntaravikalpāt sādhyadharmavikalpaṃ prasañjayato vikalpasamaḥ / kriyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ kiṃcid guru yathā loṣṭaḥ kiṃcil laghu yathā vāyuḥ evaṃ kriyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ kiṃcit kriyāvat syād yathā loṣṭaḥ kiṃcid akriyaṃ yathātmā viśeṣo vā vācya iti / hetvādyavayavasāmarthyayogī dharmaḥ sādhyaḥ taṃ dṛṣṭānte prasañjayataḥ sādhyasamaḥ / yadi yathā loṣṭas tathātmā prāptas tarhi yathātmā tathā loṣṭa iti / sādhyaś cāyam ātmā kriyāvān iti kāmaṃ loṣṭo 'pi sādhyaḥ atha naivaṃ na tarhi yathā loṣṭaḥ tathātmā //
body.translated_text: Transferring the property of the example to the thesis is the <s>utkarṣa-sama</s> (superiority-equal): 'If the <s>ātman</s> has action because of possessing action-cause-quality like a clod, then it should also be tangible like a clod; if it is not tangible, then it should not have action like a clod either — or else the difference should be stated.' Transferring the absence of a property from the thesis to the example is the <s>apakarṣa-sama</s> (inferiority-equal): 'A clod is observed to be active and non-pervading; let the <s>ātman</s> also be active and non-pervading — or else the difference should be stated.' What is to be illuminated is <s>varṇya</s>, and the contrary is <s>avarṇya</s>; these two arise when the properties of thesis and example are reversed — they are the <s>varṇya-avarṇya-samau</s>. The <s>vikalpa-sama</s> (alternative-equal) arises when, due to the differentiation of another property in the example possessing the probative property, one implies differentiation of the thesis-property: 'Something possessing action-cause-quality is heavy, like a clod; something is light, like wind. Thus something possessing action-cause-quality may have action, like a clod, or may lack action, like the <s>ātman</s> — or else the difference should be stated.' The <s>sādhya-sama</s> (what-is-to-be-proved-equal) transfers to the example a property requiring proof through the power of the members of the syllogism: 'If the <s>ātman</s> is like a clod, then the clod should be like the <s>ātman</s>; the <s>ātman</s> having action is what is to be proved; let the clod also require proof. If not, then the <s>ātman</s> is not like a clod.'

children.text: dṛṣṭāntadharmaṃ sādhye samāsañjayata utkarśasamaḥ / yadi kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yogāl loṣṭavat kriyāvān ātmā loṣṭavad eva sparśavān api prāpnoti / atha na sparśavāṃl loṣṭavat kriyāvān api na prāpnoti viparyaye vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti / sādhye dharma-abhāvaṃ dṛṣṭāntāt prasañjayato 'pakarśasamaḥ / loṣṭaḥ khalu kriyāvān avibhur dṛṣṭaḥ kāmam ātma āpi kriyāvān avibhur astu viparyaye vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti / khyāpanīyo varṇyo viparyayād avarṇyaḥ tāv etau sādhya-dṛṣṭānta-dharmau viparyasyato varṇyāvarṇyasamau bhavataḥ / sādhana-dharma-yukte dṛṣṭānte dharma-antara-vikalpāt sādhya-dharma-vikalpaṃ prasañjayato vikalpasamaḥ / kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yuktaṃ kiṃcid guru yathā loṣṭaḥ kiṃcil laghu yathā vāyuḥ evaṃ kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yuktaṃ kiṃcit kriyāvat syād yathā loṣṭaḥ kiṃcid akriyaṃ yathā ātmā viśeṣo vā vācya iti / hetv-ādy-avayava-sāmarthya-yogī dharmaḥ sādhyaḥ taṃ dṛṣṭānte prasañjayataḥ sādhyasamaḥ / yadi yathā loṣṭas tathā ātmā prāptas tarhi yathā ātmā tathā loṣṭa iti / sādhyaś ca ayam ātmā kriyāvān iti kāmaṃ loṣṭo 'pi sādhyaḥ atha na evaṃ na tarhi yathā loṣṭaḥ tathā ātmā //

body.text: eteṣām uttaram
body.translated_text: The answer to these is:

children.text: eteṣām uttaram

body.text: kiṃcitsādharmyād upasaṃhārasiddher vaidharmyād apratiṣedhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because the positive correlation is established through partial similarity, there is no refutation through dissimilarity.

children.text: kiṃcit-sādharmyād upasaṃhāra-siddher vaidharmyād apratiṣedhaḥ //

body.text: alabhyaḥ siddhasya nihnavaḥ / siddhaṃ ca kiṃcitsādhatmyād upamānaṃ yathā gaus tathā gavaya iti tatra na labhyo gogavayayor dharmavikalpaś codayitum / evaṃ sādhake dharme dṛṣṭāntādisāmarthyayukte na labhyaḥ sādhyadṛṣṭāntayor dharmavikalpād vaidharmyāt pratiṣedho vaktum iti //
body.translated_text: The concealment of what is established is not possible. What is established through partial similarity is the basis of comparison — just as 'a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow.' There, one cannot raise the objection of property-differentiation between cow and wild ox. Similarly, when the probative property is equipped with the power of the example and the rest, it is not possible to raise a refutation through property-differentiation or dissimilarity between the thesis and the example.

children.text: alabhyaḥ siddhasya nihnavaḥ / siddhaṃ ca kiṃcit-sādhatmyād upamānaṃ yathā gaus tathā gavaya iti tatra na labhyo go-gavayayor dharma-vikalpaś codayitum / evaṃ sādhake dharme dṛṣṭānta-ādi-sāmarthya-yukte na labhyaḥ sādhya-dṛṣṭāntayor dharma-vikalpād vaidharmyāt pratiṣedho vaktum iti //

body.text: sādhyātideśāc ca dṛṣṭāntopapatteḥ //
body.translated_text: And because of the cogency of the example through the transfer from what is to be proved.

children.text: sādhya-atideśāc ca dṛṣṭānta-upapatteḥ //

body.text: yatra laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ buddhisāmyaṃ tenāviparīto 'rtho 'tidiśyate prajñāpanārtham / evaṃ sādhyātideśād dṛṣṭānte upapadyamāne sādhyatvam anupapannam iti //
body.translated_text: Where there is agreement in the understanding of ordinary people and critical examiners, thereby the correct meaning is indicated for the purpose of instruction. Thus, when the example is tenable through transfer from what is to be proved, the claim that it too requires proof is untenable.

children.text: yatra laukika-parīkṣakāṇāṃ buddhi-sāmyaṃ tena aviparīto 'rtho 'tidiśyate prajñāpana-artham / evaṃ sādhya-atideśād dṛṣṭānte upapadyamāne sādhyatvam anupapannam iti //

body.text: prāpya sādhyam aprāpya vā hetoḥ prāptyāviśiṣṭatvād aprāptyāsādhakatvāc ca prāptyaprāptisamau //
body.translated_text: Whether the reason reaches or does not reach the thesis — because of non-distinction through attainment and because of non-proving through non-attainment, the <s>prāpti-sama</s> and <s>aprāpti-sama</s> arise.

children.text: prāpya sādhyam aprāpya vā hetoḥ prāptya āviśiṣṭatvād aprāptya āsādhakatvāc ca prāpty-aprāptisamau //

body.text: hetuḥ prāpya vā sādhyaṃ sādhayed aprāpya vā ? na tāvat prāpya prāptyām aviśiṣṭatvād asādhakaḥ / dvayor vidyamānayoḥ prāptau satyāṃ kiṃ kasya sādhakaṃ sādhyaṃ vā ? aprāpya sādhakaṃ na bhavati nāprāptaḥ pradīpaḥ prakāśayatīti / prāptyā pratyavasthānaṃ prāptisamaḥ aprāptyā pratyavasthānam aprāptisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Does the reason prove the thesis by reaching it or by not reaching it? Not by reaching it — because when both are present, since attainment already exists, it is non-proving: when both exist and there is attainment, what is the prover and what is to be proved? Nor does it prove without reaching — an unattained lamp does not illuminate. An objection through attainment is the <s>prāpti-sama</s> (attainment-equal); an objection through non-attainment is the <s>aprāpti-sama</s> (non-attainment-equal).

children.text: hetuḥ prāpya vā sādhyaṃ sādhayed aprāpya vā ? na tāvat prāpya prāptyām aviśiṣṭatvād asādhakaḥ / dvayor vidyamānayoḥ prāptau satyāṃ kiṃ kasya sādhakaṃ sādhyaṃ vā ? aprāpya sādhakaṃ na bhavati na aprāptaḥ pradīpaḥ prakāśayati iti / prāptyā pratyavasthānaṃ prāptisamaḥ aprāptyā pratyavasthānam aprāptisamaḥ //

body.text: anayor uttaram
body.translated_text: The answer to these two is:

children.text: anayor uttaram

body.text: ghaṭādiniṣpattidarśanāt pīḍane cābhicārād apratiṣedhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because we observe the production of pots and the like, and because of the [analogy of] harm through sorcery, there is no refutation.

children.text: ghaṭa-ādi-niṣpatti-darśanāt pīḍane ca abhicārād apratiṣedhaḥ //

body.text: ubhayathā khalv ayuktaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ kartṛkaraṇādhikaraṇāni prāpya mṛdaṃ ghaṭādikāryaṃ niṣpādayanti abhicārāc ca pīḍane sati dṛṣṭam aprāpya sādhakatvam iti //
body.translated_text: In both ways the refutation is unfounded: the agent, the instrument, and the locus produce the effect of a pot and the like by reaching the clay; and it is observed that sorcery produces harm without reaching — thus there is proving without attainment.

children.text: ubhayathā khalv ayuktaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ kartṛ-karaṇa-adhikaraṇāni prāpya mṛdaṃ ghaṭa-ādi-kāryaṃ niṣpādayanti abhicārāc ca pīḍane sati dṛṣṭam aprāpya sādhakatvam iti //

body.text: dṛṣṭāntasya kāraṇānapadeśāt pratyavasthānāc ca pratidṛṣṭāntena prasaṅgapratidṛṣṭāntasamau//
body.translated_text: Because no reason is indicated for the example, and because of the objection [by counter-example], the <s>prasaṅga-sama</s> and <s>pratidṛṣṭānta-sama</s> arise through implication and counter-example.

children.text: dṛṣṭāntasya kāraṇa-anapadeśāt pratyavasthānāc ca pratidṛṣṭāntena prasaṅga-pratidṛṣṭāntasamau//

body.text: sādhanasyāpi sādhanaṃ vaktavyam iti prasaṅgena pratyavasthānaṃ prasaṅgasamaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / kriyāhetuguṇayogī kriyāvāṃl loṣṭa iti hetur nāpadiśyate na ca hetum antereṇa siddhir astīti / pratidṛṣṭāntena pratyavasthānaṃ pratidṛṣṭāntasamaḥ / kriyāvān ātmā kriyāhetuguṇayogād loṣṭavad ity ukte pratidṛṣṭānta upādīyate -- kriyāhetuguṇayuktam ākāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ dṛṣṭam iti kaḥ punar ākāśasya kriyāhetuguṇaḥ ? vāyunā saṃyogaḥ saṃskārāpekṣaḥ vāyuvanaspatisaṃyogavad iti //
body.translated_text: The objection that a proof must also be given for the proof itself is the <s>prasaṅga-sama</s> (implication-equal) refutation: 'A clod has action because of possessing action-cause-quality — but the reason for this is not indicated, and without a reason there is no establishment.' The objection through a counter-example is the <s>pratidṛṣṭānta-sama</s> (counter-example-equal): When it is said 'The <s>ātman</s> has action because of possessing action-cause-quality, like a clod,' a counter-example is produced — 'Space possesses action-cause-quality yet is observed to be without action.' But what is the action-cause-quality of space? It is connection with wind, dependent on residual impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>), like the connection of wind with trees.

children.text: sādhanasya api sādhanaṃ vaktavyam iti prasaṅgena pratyavasthānaṃ prasaṅgasamaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yogī kriyāvāṃl loṣṭa iti hetur na apadiśyate na ca hetum antereṇa siddhir asti iti / pratidṛṣṭāntena pratyavasthānaṃ pratidṛṣṭāntasamaḥ / kriyāvān ātmā kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yogād loṣṭavad ity ukte pratidṛṣṭānta upādīyate --- kriyā-hetu-guṇa-yuktam ākāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ dṛṣṭam iti kaḥ punar ākāśasya kriyā-hetu-guṇaḥ ? vāyunā saṃyogaḥ saṃskāra-apekṣaḥ vāyu-vanaspati-saṃyogavad iti //

body.text: anayor uttaram
body.translated_text: The answer to these two is:

children.text: anayor uttaram

body.text: pradīpopādānaprasaṅgavinivṛttivat tadvinivṛttiḥ //
body.translated_text: Just as the infinite regress of fuel for a lamp is averted, so is this averted.

children.text: pradīpa-upādāna-prasaṅga-vinivṛttivat tad-vinivṛttiḥ //

body.text: idaṃ tāvad ayaṃ pṛṣṭo vaktum arhati atha ke pradīpam upādadate kimarthaṃ veti ? didṛkṣamāṇā dṛśyadarśanārtham iti / atha pradīpaṃ didṛkṣamāṇāḥ pradīpāntaraṃ kasmān nopādadate ? antareṇāpi pradīpāntataṃ dṛśyate pradīpaḥ tatra pradīpadarśanārthaṃ pradīpopādānaṃ nirarthakam / atha dṛṣṭāntaḥ kimartham ucyata iti aprajñātasya jñāpanārtham iti / atha dṛṣṭānte kāraṇāpadeśaḥ kimarthaṃ deśyate[mṛgyate] ? yadi prajñāpanārthaṃ prajñāto dṛṣṭāntaḥ / sa khalu "laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ yasminn arthe buddhisāmyaṃ sa dṛṣṭānta" iti tatprajñāpanārthaḥ kāraṇāpadeśo nirarthaka iti prasaṅgasamasyottaram //
body.translated_text: Now, this [opponent] being asked should be willing to say: who takes up a lamp, and for what purpose? Those wishing to see, for the purpose of seeing visible things. But do those wishing to see the lamp take up another lamp? Even without another lamp, the lamp is seen — therefore taking up a lamp to see the lamp is purposeless. Then for what purpose is an example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) stated? For making known what is not [yet] known. Then for what purpose is the statement of cause pointed out [or sought] in the example? If [you say] for the purpose of making known, [then] the example is already known. Indeed, 'an example is that in which ordinary examiners have a common understanding' — therefore the statement of cause for making that known is purposeless. This is the answer to the problem of implication (<s>prasaṅgasama</s>).

children.text: idaṃ tāvad ayaṃ pṛṣṭo vaktum arhati atha ke pradīpam upādadate kim-arthaṃ va īti ? didṛkṣamāṇā dṛśya-darśana-artham iti / atha pradīpaṃ didṛkṣamāṇāḥ pradīpa-antaraṃ kasmān na upādadate ? antareṇa api pradīpa-antataṃ dṛśyate pradīpaḥ tatra pradīpa-darśana-arthaṃ pradīpa-upādānaṃ nirarthakam / atha dṛṣṭāntaḥ kim-artham ucyata iti aprajñātasya jñāpana-artham iti / atha dṛṣṭānte kāraṇa-apadeśaḥ kim-arthaṃ deśyate[mṛgyate] ? yadi prajñāpana-arthaṃ prajñāto dṛṣṭāntaḥ / sa khalu "laukika-parīkṣakāṇāṃ yasminn arthe buddhi-sāmyaṃ sa dṛṣṭānta" iti tat-prajñāpana-arthaḥ kāraṇa-apadeśo nirarthaka iti prasaṅgasamasya uttaram //

body.text: atha pratidṛṣṭāntasamasyottaram
body.translated_text: Now the answer to the problem of the counter-example (<s>pratidṛṣṭānta</s>).

children.text: atha pratidṛṣṭāntasamasya uttaram

body.text: pratidṛṣṭāntahetutve ca nāhetur dṛṣṭāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: And if the counter-example were a reason, then the example would not be a non-reason.

children.text: pratidṛṣṭānta-hetutve ca na ahetur dṛṣṭāntaḥ //

body.text: pratidṛṣṭāntaṃ bruvatā na viśeṣahetur apadiśyate anena prakāreṇa pratidṛṣṭānataḥ sādhako na dṛṣṭānta iti / evaṃ pratidṛṣṭāntahetutve nāhetur dṛṣṭānta ity upapadyate / sa ca kathaṃ hetur na syāt ? yady apratiṣiddhaḥ sādhakaḥ syād iti //
body.translated_text: By one stating a counter-example, no distinctive reason is pointed out [to the effect that] 'in this manner, the counter-example is a proof, so the example is not [a valid] example.' Thus, when the counter-example is [asserted to be] a reason, 'the example is not a non-reason' is established. And how could it not be a reason? [Only] if, being unrefuted, it were a valid proof.

children.text: pratidṛṣṭāntaṃ bruvatā na viśeṣahetur apadiśyate anena prakāreṇa pratidṛṣṭānataḥ sādhako na dṛṣṭānta iti / evaṃ pratidṛṣṭānta-hetutve na ahetur dṛṣṭānta ity upapadyate / sa ca kathaṃ hetur na syāt ? yady apratiṣiddhaḥ sādhakaḥ syād iti //

body.text: prāg utpatteḥ kāraṇābhāvād anutpattisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Prior to origination, because of the absence of cause — [this is] the non-origination fallacy (<s>anutpattisama</s>).

children.text: prāg utpatteḥ kāraṇa-abhāvād anutpattisamaḥ //

body.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad ity ukte apara āha -- prāg utpatter anutpanne śabde prayatnānantarīyakatvam anityatvakāraṇaṃ nāsti, tadabhāvān nityatvaṃ prāptaṃ, nityasya cotpattir nāsti / anutpattyā pratyavasthānam anutpattisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: When it is stated that 'Sound is impermanent, because it is produced by effort, like a pot,' another says: prior to origination, when sound has not yet arisen, the property of being produced by effort — the cause of impermanence — does not exist. In its absence, permanence is obtained, and there is no origination of what is permanent. Standing firm through non-origination — [this is] the non-origination fallacy (<s>anutpattisama</s>).

children.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad ity ukte apara āha --- prāg utpatter anutpanne śabde prayatna-ānantarīyakatvam anityatva-kāraṇaṃ na asti, tad-abhāvān nityatvaṃ prāptaṃ, nityasya ca utpattir na asti / anutpattyā pratyavasthānam anutpattisamaḥ //

body.text: asyottaram
body.translated_text: Its answer:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: tathābhāvād utpannasya kāraṇopapatter na kāraṇapratiṣedhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of such a state, since the cause is established for what has arisen, there is no negation of the cause.

children.text: tathā-bhāvād utpannasya kāraṇa-upapatter na kāraṇa-pratiṣedhaḥ //

body.text: tathābhāvād utpannasyeti / utpannaḥ khalv ayaṃ śabda iti bhavati / prāg utapatteḥ śabda eva nāsti, utpannasya śabdabhāvāc chabdasya sataḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvam anityatvakāraṇam upapadyate, kāraṇopapatter ayukto 'yaṃ doṣaḥ "prāg utpatteḥ kāraṇābhāvād" iti //
body.translated_text: 'Because of such a state, for what has arisen' — this sound has indeed arisen, such is the case. Prior to origination there is simply no sound; for the arisen sound, i.e. for the existing sound, the property of being produced by effort serves as a cause of impermanence. Because the cause is established, the objection 'prior to origination there is absence of cause' is unfounded.

children.text: tathā-bhāvād utpannasya iti / utpannaḥ khalv ayaṃ śabda iti bhavati / prāg utapatteḥ śabda eva na asti, utpannasya śabda-bhāvāc chabdasya sataḥ prayatna-ānantarīyakatvam anityatva-kāraṇam upapadyate, kāraṇa upapatter ayukto 'yaṃ doṣaḥ "prāg utpatteḥ kāraṇa-abhāvād" iti //

body.text: sāmānya+dṛṣṭāntayor aindriyakatve samāne nityānityasādharmyāt saṃśayasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because sense-perceptibility is common to both the general [term] and the example, because of similarity with both permanent and impermanent — [this is] the doubt-fallacy (<s>saṃśayasama</s>).

children.text: sāmānya+dṛṣṭāntayor aindriyakatve samāne nitya-anitya-sādharmyāt saṃśayasamaḥ //

body.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad ity ukte hetau saṃśayena pratyavatiṣṭate -- sati prayatnānantarīyakatve asty evāsya nityena sāmānyena sādharmyam aindriyakatvam, asti ca ghaṭenānityena, ato nityānityasādharmyād anivṛttiḥ saṃśaya iti //
body.translated_text: When it is stated that 'Sound is impermanent, because it is produced by effort, like a pot,' [the opponent] stands firm through doubt regarding the reason: given that [sound] is produced by effort, there exists similarity with a permanent [entity] through the common property of sense-perceptibility, and there also exists [similarity] with an impermanent pot — therefore, because of similarity with both permanent and impermanent, there is no resolution: [this is] the doubt.

children.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad ity ukte hetau saṃśayena pratyavatiṣṭate --- sati prayatna-ānantarīyakatve asty eva asya nityena sāmānyena sādharmyam aindriyakatvam, asti ca ghaṭena anityena, ato nitya-anitya-sādharmyād anivṛttiḥ saṃśaya iti //

body.text: asyottaram
body.translated_text: Its answer:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: sādharmyāt saṃśaye na saṃśayo vaidharmyād ubhayathā vā saṃśaye 'tyantasaṃśayaprasaṅgo nityatvānabhyupagamāc ca sāmānysyāpratiṣedhaḥ //
body.translated_text: When there is doubt from similarity, there is no [real] doubt because of dissimilarity; or if there is doubt either way, there would be the absurdity of perpetual doubt; and because permanence is not accepted [for sound], the common [property] is not negated.

children.text: sādharmyāt saṃśaye na saṃśayo vaidharmyād ubhayathā vā saṃśaye 'tyanta-saṃśaya-prasaṅgo nityatva-anabhyupagamāc ca sāmānysya apratiṣedhaḥ //

body.text: viśeṣād vaidharmyād avadhāryamāṇe 'rthe puruṣa iti, na sthāṇupuruṣasādharmyāt saṃśayo 'vakāśaṃ labhate / evaṃ vaidharmyād viśeṣāt prayatnānantarīyakatvād avadhāryamāṇe śabdasyānityatve nityānityasādharmyāt saṃśayo 'vakāśaṃ na labhate / yadi vai labhate, tataḥ sthāṇupuruṣasādharmyānucchedād atyantaṃ saṃśayaḥ syāt / gṛhyamāṇe ca viśeṣe nityaṃ sādharmyaṃ saṃśayahetur iti nābhyupagamyate / na hi gṛhyamāṇe puruṣasya viśeṣe sthāṇupuruṣasādharmyaṃ saṃśayahetur bhavati //
body.translated_text: When the object is ascertained through the distinguishing [property] of dissimilarity — 'this is a person' — then the doubt from the similarity of a post and a person does not find scope. Likewise, when the impermanence of sound is ascertained through the distinguishing [property] of dissimilarity, namely being produced by effort, the doubt from similarity with both permanent and impermanent does not find scope. For if it did find scope, then from the unbroken similarity of post and person, there would be perpetual doubt. And when the distinguishing feature is grasped, the permanent similarity is not accepted as a cause of doubt. For when the distinguishing feature of the person is grasped, the similarity of post and person does not serve as a cause of doubt.

children.text: viśeṣād vaidharmyād avadhāryamāṇe 'rthe puruṣa iti, na sthāṇu-puruṣa-sādharmyāt saṃśayo 'vakāśaṃ labhate / evaṃ vaidharmyād viśeṣāt prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād avadhāryamāṇe śabdasya anityatve nitya anitya-sādharmyāt saṃśayo 'vakāśaṃ na labhate / yadi vai labhate, tataḥ sthāṇu-puruṣa-sādharmya-anucchedād atyantaṃ saṃśayaḥ syāt / gṛhyamāṇe ca viśeṣe nityaṃ sādharmyaṃ saṃśaya-hetur iti na abhyupagamyate / na hi gṛhyamāṇe puruṣasya viśeṣe sthāṇu-puruṣa-sādharmyaṃ saṃśaya-hetur bhavati //

body.text: ubhayasādharmyāt prakriyāsiddheḥ prakaraṇasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of the establishment of the procedure through similarity with both, [this is] the topic-fallacy (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>).

children.text: ubhaya-sādharmyāt prakriyā-siddheḥ prakaraṇasamaḥ //

body.text: ubhayena nityena cānityena ca sādharmyāt pakṣapratipakṣayoḥ pravṛttiḥ prakriyā / anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad ity ekaḥ pakṣaṃ pravarttayati, dvitīyaś ca nityasādharmyāt pratipakṣaṃ pravarttayati -- nityaḥ śabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvāc chabdatvavad iti / evaṃ ca sati prayatnānantarīyakatvād iti hetur anityasādharmyeṇa ucyamāno na prakaraṇam ativarttate , prakaraṇānativṛtter nirṇayānativartanam / samānaṃ caitan nityasādharmyeṇocyamāṇe hetau / tad idaṃ prakaraṇānativṛttyā pratyavasthānaṃ prakaraṇasamaḥ / samānaṃ caitad vaidharmye 'pi, ubhayavaidharmyāt prakriyāsiddheḥ prakaraṇasama iti //
body.translated_text: Because of similarity with both — permanent and impermanent — the procedure (<s>prakriyā</s>) consists in the operation of both thesis and counter-thesis. One advances the thesis 'Sound is impermanent, because it is produced by effort, like a pot.' Another advances the counter-thesis through similarity with the permanent: 'Sound is permanent, because it is audible, like sound-ness.' In this case, the reason stated through similarity with the impermanent — 'because it is produced by effort' — does not go beyond the topic (<s>prakaraṇa</s>); from not going beyond the topic, there is no going beyond the determination. And the same applies when the reason is stated through similarity with the permanent. This standing firm through not going beyond the topic is the topic-fallacy (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>). And the same applies to dissimilarity: because of the establishment of the procedure through dissimilarity with both, [it is also] a topic-fallacy.

children.text: ubhayena nityena ca anityena ca sādharmyāt pakṣa-pratipakṣayoḥ pravṛttiḥ prakriyā / anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad ity ekaḥ pakṣaṃ pravarttayati, dvitīyaś ca nitya-sādharmyāt pratipakṣaṃ pravarttayati --- nityaḥ śabdaḥ śrāvaṇatvāc chabdatvavad iti / evaṃ ca sati prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād iti hetur anitya-sādharmyeṇa ucyamāno na prakaraṇam ativarttate , prakaraṇa-anativṛtter nirṇaya-anativartanam / samānaṃ ca etan nitya-sādharmyeṇa ucyamāṇe hetau / tad idaṃ prakaraṇa-anativṛttyā pratyavasthānaṃ prakaraṇasamaḥ / samānaṃ ca etad vaidharmye 'pi, ubhaya-vaidharmyāt prakriyā-siddheḥ prakaraṇasama iti //

body.text: pratipakṣāt prakaraṇasiddheḥ pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ pratipakṣopapatteḥ //
body.translated_text: From the counter-thesis, because of the establishment of the topic, the impossibility of refutation is [established] because of the possibility of the counter-thesis.

children.text: pratipakṣāt prakaraṇa-siddheḥ pratiṣedha-anupapattiḥ pratipakṣa upapatteḥ //

body.text: ubhayasādharmyāt prakriyāsiddhaṃ bruvatā pratipakṣāt prakriyāsiddhir uktā bhavati / yady ubhayasādharmyaṃ, tatra ekataraḥ pratipakṣa ity evaṃ saty upapannaḥ pratipakṣo bhavati / pratipakṣopapatter anupapannaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ, yadi pratipakṣopapattiḥ pratiṣedho nopapadyate, atha pratiṣedhopapattiḥ pratipakṣo nopapadyate, pratipakṣopapattiḥ pratiṣedhopapattiś ceti vipratiṣiddham iti / tattvānavadhāraṇāc ca prakriyāsiddhir viparyaye prakaraṇāvasānāt, tattvāvadhāraṇe hy avasitaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhavatīti //
body.translated_text: By one who says that the procedure is established through similarity with both, the establishment of the procedure through the counter-thesis has been stated. If there is similarity with both, then one of them is the counter-thesis — and thus the counter-thesis is established. Because of the establishment of the counter-thesis, the refutation is not established. If the counter-thesis is established, then refutation is not established; if refutation is established, then the counter-thesis is not established — [to say both are established is] contradictory. And because the truth is not ascertained, the procedure is established in the reverse case, since the topic ends [there]; for when truth is ascertained, the topic is concluded.

children.text: ubhaya-sādharmyāt prakriyā-siddhaṃ bruvatā pratipakṣāt prakriyā-siddhir uktā bhavati / yady ubhaya-sādharmyaṃ, tatra ekataraḥ pratipakṣa ity evaṃ saty upapannaḥ pratipakṣo bhavati / pratipakṣa-upapatter anupapannaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ, yadi pratipakṣa-upapattiḥ pratiṣedho na upapadyate, atha pratiṣedha-upapattiḥ pratipakṣo na upapadyate, pratipakṣa-upapattiḥ pratiṣedha-upapattiś ca iti vipratiṣiddham iti / tattva anavadhāraṇāc ca prakriyā-siddhir viparyaye prakaraṇa avasānāt, tattva-avadhāraṇe hy avasitaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhavati iti //

body.text: traikālyāsiddher hetor ahetusamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because the reason is not established in any of the three times — [this is] the non-reason fallacy (<s>ahetusama</s>).

children.text: traikālya-asiddher hetor ahetusamaḥ //

body.text: hetuḥ sādhanam, tat sādhyāt pūrvaṃ paścāt saha vā bhavet / yadi pūrvaṃ sādhanam, asati sādhye kasya sādhanam ? atha paścād, asati sādhane kasyedaṃ sādhyam ? atha yugapat sādhyasādane, dvayor vidyamānayoḥ kiṃ kasya sādhanaṃ kiṃ kasya sādhyam iti hetur ahetunā na viśiṣyate / ahetunā sādharmyāt prayavasthānam ahetusamaḥ //
body.translated_text: The reason is the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>). It must be prior to, subsequent to, or simultaneous with what is to be proved. If the means of proof is prior, then in the absence of what is to be proved, what does it prove? If subsequent, then in the absence of the means of proof, of what is this the object of proof? If the means of proof and the object of proof are simultaneous, then when both exist, what is the means of proof for what, and what is the object of proof for what? — thus the reason is not distinguished from a non-reason. Standing firm through similarity with a non-reason — [this is] the non-reason fallacy (<s>ahetusama</s>).

children.text: hetuḥ sādhanam, tat sādhyāt pūrvaṃ paścāt saha vā bhavet / yadi pūrvaṃ sādhanam, asati sādhye kasya sādhanam ? atha paścād, asati sādhane kasya idaṃ sādhyam ? atha yugapat sādhya-sādane, dvayor vidyamānayoḥ kiṃ kasya sādhanaṃ kiṃ kasya sādhyam iti hetur ahetunā na viśiṣyate / ahetunā sādharmyāt prayavasthānam ahetusamaḥ //

body.text: na hetutaḥ sādhyasiddhes traikālyāsiddhiḥ //
body.translated_text: There is no [problem of] non-establishment in the three times, because what is to be proved is established through the reason.

children.text: na hetutaḥ sādhya-siddhes traikālya-asiddhiḥ //

body.text: na traikālyāsiddhiḥ / kasmāt ? hetutaḥ sādhyasiddheḥ / nirvartanīyasya nirvṛttir vijñeyasya vijñānam ubhayaṃ kāraṇato dṛśyate, so 'yaṃ mahān pratyakṣaviṣaya udāharaṇam iti / yat tu khalūktam asati sādhye kasya sādhanam iti ? yat tu nirvatyate yac ca vijñāpyate tasyeti //
body.translated_text: There is no non-establishment in the three times. Why? Because what is to be proved is established through the reason. The production of what is to be produced, and the knowledge of what is to be known — both are seen from the cause. This is a great matter within the domain of direct perception — such is the illustration. As for what was said, 'in the absence of what is to be proved, what does [the reason] prove?' — it proves that which is produced and that which is made known.

children.text: na traikālya-asiddhiḥ / kasmāt ? hetutaḥ sādhya-siddheḥ / nirvartanīyasya nirvṛttir vijñeyasya vijñānam ubhayaṃ kāraṇato dṛśyate, so 'yaṃ mahān pratyakṣa-viṣaya udāharaṇam iti / yat tu khalu uktam asati sādhye kasya sādhanam iti ? yat tu nirvatyate yac ca vijñāpyate tasya iti //

body.text: pratiṣedānupapatteś ca pratiṣeddhavyāpratiṣedhaḥ //
body.translated_text: And because of the impossibility of refutation, what is to be refuted is [itself] not refuted.

children.text: pratiṣeda-anupapatteś ca pratiṣeddhavya apratiṣedhaḥ //

body.text: pūrvaṃ paścād yugapad vā pratiṣedha iti nopapadyate, pratiṣedhānupapatteḥ sthāpanāhetuḥ siddha iti //
body.translated_text: Refutation prior to, subsequent to, or simultaneous [with what is refuted] is not established. Because of the impossibility of refutation, the reason for establishment (<s>sthāpanā</s>) is proven.

children.text: pūrvaṃ paścād yugapad vā pratiṣedha iti na upapadyate, pratiṣedha anupapatteḥ sthāpanā-hetuḥ siddha iti //

body.text: arthāpattitaḥ pratipakṣasiddher arthāpattisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because the counter-thesis is established by presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>) — [this is] the presumption-fallacy (<s>arthāpattisama</s>).

children.text: artha-āpattitaḥ pratipakṣa-siddher arthāpattisamaḥ //

body.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad iti sthāpite pakṣe arthāpattyā pratipakṣaṃ sādhayato 'rthāpattisamaḥ / yadi prayatnānantarīyakatvād anityasādharmyād anityaḥ śabda iti, arthād āpadyate nityasādharmyān nitya iti, asti cāsya nityena sādharmyam asparśatvam iti //
body.translated_text: When the thesis 'Sound is impermanent, because it is produced by effort, like a pot' is established, one who establishes the counter-thesis by presumption [commits] the presumption-fallacy. [The objection runs:] if sound is impermanent because of similarity with the impermanent through being produced by effort, then by implication (<s>arthāpatti</s>) it follows that [sound] is permanent because of similarity with the permanent — and it does indeed have similarity with the permanent, namely intangibility.

children.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavad iti sthāpite pakṣe artha-āpattyā pratipakṣaṃ sādhayato 'rthāpattisamaḥ / yadi prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād anitya-sādharmyād anityaḥ śabda iti, arthād āpadyate nitya-sādharmyān nitya iti, asti ca asya nityena sādharmyam asparśatvam iti //

body.text: asyottaram
body.translated_text: Its answer:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: anuktasyārthāpatteḥ pakṣahāner upapattir anuktatvād anaikānatikatvāc cārthāpatteḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of the abandonment of the [opponent's own] thesis through a presumption that is [itself] unstated, there is establishment [of the original thesis]; because [the presumption is] unstated, and because presumption is not one-sided.

children.text: anuktasya artha-āpatteḥ pakṣa-hāner upapattir anuktatvād anaikānatikatvāc ca artha-āpatteḥ //

body.text: anupapādya sāmarthyam anuktam arthād āpadyate iti bruvataḥ pakṣahāner upapattir anuktatvāt, anityapakṣasiddhāv arthād āpannaṃ nityapakṣasya hānir iti / anaikānatikatvāc cārthāpatteḥ / ubhayapakṣasamā ceyam arthāpattiḥ / yadi nityasādharmyād asparśatvād ākāśavac ca nityaḥ śabdaḥ, arthād āpanna, anityasādharmyāt prayatnānantarīyakatvād anitya iti / na ceyaṃ viparyayamātrād ekāntenārthāpattiḥ / na khalu vai ghaṇasya grāvṇaḥ patanam ity arthād āpadyate -- dravāṇām apāṃ patanābhāva iti //
body.translated_text: One who, without establishing its capability and without stating it, says 'it follows by implication' — for him there is the establishment of the abandonment of his own thesis, because it is unstated. For when the thesis of impermanence is established, what follows by implication is the abandonment of the thesis of permanence. And this presumption applies equally to both theses. If sound is permanent because of similarity with the permanent through intangibility, like space, then by implication from similarity with the impermanent through being produced by effort, it is impermanent. And this presumption is not one-sided merely from the reversal. For indeed it does not follow by implication from the falling of a lump of stone that there is no falling of liquids like water.

children.text: anupapādya sāmarthyam anuktam arthād āpadyate iti bruvataḥ pakṣa-hāner upapattir anuktatvāt, anitya-pakṣa-siddhāv arthād āpannaṃ nitya-pakṣasya hānir iti / anaikānatikatvāc ca artha-āpatteḥ / ubhaya-pakṣa-samā ca iyam arthāpattiḥ / yadi nitya-sādharmyād asparśatvād ākāśavac ca nityaḥ śabdaḥ, arthād āpanna, anitya-sādharmyāt prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād anitya iti / na ca iyaṃ viparyaya-mātrād ekāntena artha-āpattiḥ / na khalu vai ghaṇasya grāvṇaḥ patanam ity arthād āpadyate --- dravāṇām apāṃ patana-abhāva iti //

body.text: ekadharmopapatter aviśeṣe sarvāviśeṣaprasaṅgāt sadbhāvopapatter aviśeṣasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because there is no distinction when one property applies, and because the property of existence applies [universally], there would be universal non-distinction — [this is] the non-distinction fallacy (<s>aviśeṣasama</s>).

children.text: eka-dharma-upapatter aviśeṣe sarva-aviśeṣa-prasaṅgāt sad-bhāva-upapatter aviśeṣasamaḥ //

body.text: eko dharmaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ śabdaghaṭayor upapadyata ity aviśeṣe ubhayor anityatve, sarvāviśeṣaḥ prasajyate / katham ? sadbhāvopapatteḥ / eko dharmaḥ sadbhāvaḥ sarvasyopapadyate, sadbhāvopapatteḥ sarvāviśeṣaprasaṅgāt pratyavasthānam aviśeṣasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: One property — being produced by effort — applies to both sound and pot, and if [this means] no distinction [between them], that they are both impermanent, then universal non-distinction follows. How? Because of the applicability of [the property of] existence. One property — existence — applies to everything; because of the applicability of existence, standing firm through [the objection of] universal non-distinction — [this is] the non-distinction fallacy (<s>aviśeṣasama</s>).

children.text: eko dharmaḥ prayatna-ānantarīyakatvaṃ śabda-ghaṭayor upapadyata ity aviśeṣe ubhayor anityatve, sarva-aviśeṣaḥ prasajyate / katham ? sad-bhāva-upapatteḥ / eko dharmaḥ sad-bhāvaḥ sarvasya upapadyate, sad-bhāva-upapatteḥ sarva-aviśeṣa-prasaṅgāt pratyavasthānam aviśeṣasamaḥ //

body.text: kvacit taddharmopapatteḥ kvacic cānupapatteḥ pratiṣedhābhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because that property sometimes applies and sometimes does not apply, there is no [valid] refutation.

children.text: kvacit tad-dharma upapatteḥ kvacic ca anupapatteḥ pratiṣedha-abhāvaḥ //

body.text: yathā sādhyadṛṣṭāntayor ekadharmasya prayatnānantarīyakatvasyopapatter anityatvaṃ dharmāntaram aviśeṣaḥ, naivaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ sadbhāvopapattinimittaṃ dharmāntaram asti, yena aviśeṣaḥ syāt / atha matam anityatvam eva dharmānataraṃ sadbhāvopapattinimittaṃ bhāvānāṃ sarvatra syād iti, evaṃ khalu vai kalpyamāne anityāḥ sarve bhāvāḥ sadbhāvopapatter iti pakṣaḥ prāpnoti / tatra pratijñārthavyatiriktam anyad udāharaṇaṃ nāsti, anudāharaṇaś ca hetur nāstīti / pratijñaikadeśasya codāharaṇatvam anupapannam, na hi sādhyam udāharaṇaṃ bhavati / sataś ca nityānityabhāvād anityatvānupapattiḥ / tasmāt sadbhāvopapatteḥ sarvāviśeṣaprasaṅga iti nirabhidheyam etad vākyam iti / sarvabhāvānāṃ sadbhāvopapatter anityatvam iti bruvatānujñātaṃ śabdasyānityatvaṃ, tatrānupapannaḥ pratiṣedha iti //
body.translated_text: Just as, in the case of the thesis and the example, there is the establishment of one property — namely, being consequent upon effort (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) — and impermanence is another property [and so there is] no [fallacious] non-distinction; in the same way, for all entities, there is no other property that serves as the ground for the establishment of existence by which there would be non-distinction. Now, if one thinks that impermanence itself is another property that would serve as the ground for the establishment of existence of entities everywhere — then indeed, when thus postulated, the thesis would follow that 'all entities are impermanent because of the establishment of existence.' In that case, there is no example other than the meaning of the thesis itself, and a reason without an example is no reason. And it is untenable for a part of the thesis to serve as the example, for what is to be proved cannot be the example. Moreover, since what exists has both eternal and non-eternal states, the establishment of impermanence fails. Therefore, the statement that 'from the establishment of existence there follows non-distinction for all' is meaningless. By one who says 'all entities are impermanent because of the establishment of existence,' the impermanence of sound has been conceded; therein, the refutation is untenable.

children.text: yathā sādhya-dṛṣṭāntayor eka-dharmasya prayatna-ānantarīyakatvasya upapatter anityatvaṃ dharma-antaram aviśeṣaḥ, na evaṃ sarva-bhāvānāṃ sad-bhāva upapatti-nimittaṃ dharma-antaram asti, yena aviśeṣaḥ syāt / atha matam anityatvam eva dharma-anataraṃ sad-bhāva-upapatti-nimittaṃ bhāvānāṃ sarvatra syād iti, evaṃ khalu vai kalpyamāne anityāḥ sarve bhāvāḥ sad-bhāva-upapatter iti pakṣaḥ prāpnoti / tatra pratijñā-artha-vyatiriktam anyad udāharaṇaṃ na asti, anudāharaṇaś ca hetur na asti iti / pratijñā-eka-deśasya ca udāharaṇatvam anupapannam, na hi sādhyam udāharaṇaṃ bhavati / sataś ca nitya anitya-bhāvād anityatva-anupapattiḥ / tasmāt sad-bhāva-upapatteḥ sarva-aviśeṣa-prasaṅga iti nirabhidheyam etad vākyam iti / sarva-bhāvānāṃ sad-bhāva-upapatter anityatvam iti bruvata ānujñātaṃ śabdasya anityatvaṃ, tatra anupapannaḥ pratiṣedha iti //

body.text: ubhayakāraṇopapatter upapattisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of the establishment of both [types of] causes, [this is the fallacy called] <s>upapattisamaḥ</s> (the balancing of evidence).

children.text: ubhaya-kāraṇa-upapatter upapattisamaḥ //

body.text: yady anityatvakāraṇam upapadyate śabdasyety anityaḥ śabdo nityatvakāraṇam apy upapadyate 'syāsparśatvam iti nityatvam apy upapadyate / ubhayasyānityatvasya nityatvasya ca kāraṇopapattyā pratyavasthānam upapattisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: If the cause of impermanence is established for sound — and therefore sound is impermanent — then the cause of eternality, namely its intangibility (<s>asparśatva</s>), is also established for it, and so eternality too is established. The counter-objection through the establishment of causes for both — impermanence and eternality — is [the fallacy called] <s>upapattisamaḥ</s> (the balancing of evidence).

children.text: yady anityatva-kāraṇam upapadyate śabdasya ity anityaḥ śabdo nityatva-kāraṇam apy upapadyate 'sya asparśatvam iti nityatvam apy upapadyate / ubhayasya anityatvasya nityatvasya ca kāraṇa-upapattyā pratyavasthānam upapattisamaḥ //

body.text: upapattikāraṇābhyanujñānād apratiṣedhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of the concession of the establishment of the cause, there is no refutation.

children.text: upapatti-kāraṇa-abhyanujñānād apratiṣedhaḥ //

body.text: ubhayakāraṇopapatter iti bruvatā nānityatvakāraṇopapatter anityatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, yadi pratiṣidhyate nobhayakāraṇopapattiḥ syāt / ubhayakāraṇopapattivacanād anityatvakāraṇopapattir abhyanujñāyate, abhyanujñānād anupapannaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / vyāghātāt pratiṣedha iti cet, samāno vyāghātaḥ / ekasya nityatvānityatvaprasaṅgaṃ vyāhataṃ bruvatoktaṃ pratiṣedha iti cet ? svapakṣaparapakṣayoḥ samāno vyāghātaḥ, sa ca naikatarasya sādhaka iti //
body.translated_text: By one who says 'because of the establishment of both [types of] causes,' the impermanence [of sound] is not refuted on account of the establishment of the cause of impermanence — for if it were refuted, there would not be the establishment of both causes. From the statement of the establishment of both causes, the establishment of the cause of impermanence is conceded; from this concession, the refutation is untenable. If one says 'the refutation is due to contradiction' — the contradiction is equal [on both sides]. One who asserts the contradictory attribution of both eternality and impermanence to a single [entity] — if one says 'that is the refutation' — the contradiction is equal in one's own position and the opponent's position, and it does not establish either one.

children.text: ubhaya-kāraṇa-upapatter iti bruvatā na anityatva-kāraṇa upapatter anityatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, yadi pratiṣidhyate na ubhaya-kāraṇa-upapattiḥ syāt / ubhaya-kāraṇa-upapatti-vacanād anityatva-kāraṇa-upapattir abhyanujñāyate, abhyanujñānād anupapannaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ / vyāghātāt pratiṣedha iti cet, samāno vyāghātaḥ / ekasya nityatva-anityatva-prasaṅgaṃ vyāhataṃ bruvata ūktaṃ pratiṣedha iti cet ? sva-pakṣa-para-pakṣayoḥ samāno vyāghātaḥ, sa ca na ekatarasya sādhaka iti //

body.text: nirdiṣṭakāraṇābhāve 'py upalambhād upalabdhisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of perception even in the absence of the stated cause, [this is the fallacy called] <s>upalabdhisamaḥ</s> (the balancing of perception).

children.text: nirdiṣṭa-kāraṇa-abhāve 'py upalambhād upalabdhisamaḥ //

body.text: nirdiṣṭasya prayatnānantarīyakatvasyānityatvakāraṇasyābhāve 'pi vāyunodanād vṛkṣaśākhābhaṅgajasya śabdasyānityatvam upalabhyate / nirdiṣṭasya sādhanasyābhāve 'pi sādhyadharmopalabdhyā pratyavasthānam upalabdhisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Even in the absence of the stated cause of impermanence — namely, being consequent upon effort (<s>prayatnānantarīyakatva</s>) — the impermanence of sound produced from the breaking of tree branches by wind-force is perceived. The counter-objection through the perception of the property to be proved even in the absence of the stated proof is [the fallacy called] <s>upalabdhisamaḥ</s> (the balancing of perception).

children.text: nirdiṣṭasya prayatna-ānantarīyakatvasya anityatva-kāraṇasya abhāve 'pi vāyu-nodanād vṛkṣa-śākhā-bhaṅga-jasya śabdasya anityatvam upalabhyate / nirdiṣṭasya sādhanasya abhāve 'pi sādhya-dharma upalabdhyā pratyavasthānam upalabdhisamaḥ //

body.text: asyottaram
body.translated_text: The answer to this:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: kāraṇāntarād api taddharmopapatter apratiṣedhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because the property in question is established even from another cause, there is no refutation.

children.text: kāraṇa-antarād api tad-dharma-upapatter apratiṣedhaḥ //

body.text: prayatnānantarīyakatvād iti bruvatā kāraṇata utpattir abhidhīyate, na kāryasya kāraṇaniyamaḥ / yadi ca kāraṇāntarād apy utpadyamānasya śabdasya tad anityatvam upapadyate, kim atra pratiṣidhyata iti //
body.translated_text: By one who says 'because of being consequent upon effort,' origination from a cause is stated, not the restriction of the effect to [only] that cause. And if the impermanence of sound is established even when it arises from another cause, what is being refuted here?

children.text: prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād iti bruvatā kāraṇata utpattir abhidhīyate, na kāryasya kāraṇa-niyamaḥ / yadi ca kāraṇa-antarād apy utpadyamānasya śabdasya tad anityatvam upapadyate, kim atra pratiṣidhyata iti //

body.text: na prāg uccāraṇād vidyamānasya śabdasyānupalabdhiḥ, kasmāt ? āvaraṇādyanupalabdheḥ / yathā vidyamānasyodakāder arthasyāvaraṇāder anupalabdhiḥ naivaṃ śabdasyāgrahaṇakāraṇenāvaranādinānupalabdhiḥ / gṛhyeta caitad asyāgrahaṇakāraṇam udakādivat, na gṛhyate / tasmād udakādiviparītaḥ śabdo 'nupalabhyamāna iti /
body.translated_text: Sound, which exists prior to utterance, is not unperceived. Why? Because of non-perception due to concealment (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) and the like. Just as there is non-perception of an existing entity such as water due to concealment and the like, so too the non-perception of sound [could be explained] by a cause of non-apprehension such as concealment. And this cause of its non-apprehension should be apprehended like [that of] water, etc. — but it is not apprehended. Therefore, sound, being unperceived, is the opposite of water, etc.

children.text: na prāg uccāraṇād vidyamānasya śabdasya anupalabdhiḥ, kasmāt ? āvaraṇa-ādy-anupalabdheḥ / yathā vidyamānasya udaka-āder arthasyā avaraṇa-āder anupalabdhiḥ na evaṃ śabdasya agrahaṇa-kāraṇenā avarana-ādina ānupalabdhiḥ / gṛhyeta ca etad asya agrahaṇa-kāraṇam udaka-ādivat, na gṛhyate / tasmād udaka-ādi-viparītaḥ śabdo 'nupalabhyamāna iti /

body.text: tadanupalabdher anupalambhād abhāvasiddhau tadviparītopapatter anupalabdhisamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of the non-perception of those [causes of non-perception], and because from non-perception the non-existence is established, and because of the establishment of the opposite of that — [this is the fallacy called] <s>anupalabdhisamaḥ</s> (the balancing of non-perception).

children.text: tad-anupalabdher anupalambhād abhāva-siddhau tad-viparīta upapatter anupalabdhisamaḥ //

body.text: teṣām āvaraṇādīnām anupalabdhir nopalabhyate / anupalambhān nāstīty abhāvo 'syāḥ sidhyati / abhāvasiddhau hetvabhāvāt tadviparītam astitvam āvaraṇādīnām avadhāryate / tadviparītopapatter yatpratijñātaṃ "na prāg uccāraṇād vidyamānasya śabdasyānupalabdhir ity" etan na sidhyati / so 'yaṃ "hetur āvaraṇādyanupalabdher" ity āvaraṇādiṣu cāvaraṇādyanupalabdhau ca samayānupalabdhyā pratyavasthito 'nupalabdhisamo bhavati //
body.translated_text: The non-perception of those — concealment and the like — is not perceived [i.e., there is no evidence of concealment]. From non-perception, the non-existence of this [concealment] is established. When non-existence is established, due to the absence of the reason [for non-perception], the opposite — namely the existence of concealment and the like — is determined. Because of the establishment of the opposite, what was asserted — 'sound, which exists prior to utterance, is not unperceived' — this is not established. This reason — 'because of non-perception of concealment and the like' — is countered regarding concealment and the like, and regarding the non-perception of concealment and the like, by a parallel non-perception, and thus becomes [the fallacy called] <s>anupalabdhisamaḥ</s> (the balancing of non-perception).

children.text: teṣām āvaraṇa-ādīnām anupalabdhir na upalabhyate / anupalambhān na asti ity abhāvo 'syāḥ sidhyati / abhāva-siddhau hetv-abhāvāt tad-viparītam astitvam āvaraṇa-ādīnām avadhāryate / tad-viparīta-upapatter yat-pratijñātaṃ "na prāg uccāraṇād vidyamānasya śabdasya anupalabdhir ity" etan na sidhyati / so 'yaṃ "hetur āvaraṇa-ādy-anupalabdher" ity āvaraṇā adiṣu cā avaraṇa-ādy-anupalabdhau ca samaya-anupalabdhyā pratyavasthito 'nupalabdhisamo bhavati //

body.text: asya uttaram
body.translated_text: The answer to this:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: anupalambhātmakatvād anupalabdher ahetuḥ //
body.translated_text: Because non-perception is of the nature of non-apprehension, [the objection] is without a valid reason.

children.text: anupalambha-ātmakatvād anupalabdher ahetuḥ //

body.text: āvaraṇādyanupalabdhir nāsti, anupalambhād ity ahetuḥ / kasmāt ? anupalambhātmakatvād anupalabdheḥ / upalambhābhāvamātratvād anupalabdheḥ / yad asti tad upalabdher viṣayaḥ, upalabdhyā tad astīti pratijñāyate / yan nāsti tad anupalabdher viṣayaḥ, anupalabhyamānaṃ nāstīti pratijñāyate / so 'yam āvaraṇādyanupalabheḥ anupalambha upalabdhyabhāve 'nupalabdhau svaviṣaye pravarttamāno na svaviṣayaṃ pratiṣedhati / apratiṣiddhā cāvaraṇādyanupalabdhi hetutvāya kalpate / āvaraṇādīni tu vidyamānatvād upalabdher viṣayāḥ, teṣām upalabdhyā bhavitavyam / yat tāni nopalabhyante, tadupalabdheḥ svaviṣayapratipādikāyā abhāvād anupalambhād anupalabdher viṣayo gamyate -- na santy āvaraṇādīni śabdasyāgrahaṇakāraṇānīti / anupalambhāt tv anupalabhiḥ sidhyati, viṣayaḥ sa tasyeti //
body.translated_text: Concealment and the like do not exist — because of non-apprehension — [this] is without a valid reason. Why? Because non-perception is of the nature of non-apprehension. Non-perception is merely the absence of apprehension. What exists is the object of apprehension, and through apprehension it is asserted 'that exists.' What does not exist is the object of non-perception, and being unperceived, it is asserted 'that does not exist.' This non-apprehension of the non-perception of concealment and the like — operating in its own domain, which is the absence of apprehension — does not negate its own domain. And the non-perception of concealment and the like, being unnegated, is fit to serve as a reason. But concealment and the like, being existent [if they existed], would be objects of apprehension, and their apprehension should occur. That they are not apprehended — from the absence of apprehension, which establishes its own domain, one infers the domain of non-perception: namely, that there are no causes of non-apprehension of sound, such as concealment and the like. But non-perception is indeed established from non-apprehension — that is its domain.

children.text: āvaraṇa-ādy-anupalabdhir na asti, anupalambhād ity ahetuḥ / kasmāt ? anupalambha-ātmakatvād anupalabdheḥ / upalambha-abhāva-mātratvād anupalabdheḥ / yad asti tad upalabdher viṣayaḥ, upalabdhyā tad asti iti pratijñāyate / yan na asti tad anupalabdher viṣayaḥ, anupalabhyamānaṃ na asti iti pratijñāyate / so 'yam āvaraṇa-ādy-anupalabheḥ anupalambha upalabdhy-abhāve 'nupalabdhau svaviṣaye pravarttamāno na svaviṣayaṃ pratiṣedhati / apratiṣiddhā cā avaraṇa-ādy-anupalabdhi hetutvāya kalpate / āvaraṇa-ādīni tu vidyamānatvād upalabdher viṣayāḥ, teṣām upalabdhyā bhavitavyam / yat tāni na upalabhyante, tad-upalabdheḥ svaviṣaya-pratipādikāyā abhāvād anupalambhād anupalabdher viṣayo gamyate --- na santy āvaraṇa-ādīni śabdasya agrahaṇa-kāraṇāni iti / anupalambhāt tv anupalabhiḥ sidhyati, viṣayaḥ sa tasya iti //

body.text: jñānavikalpānāṃ ca bhāvābhāvasaṃvedanād adhyātmam //
body.translated_text: And because of the internal awareness of the presence and absence of varieties of cognition.

children.text: jñāna-vikalpānāṃ ca bhāva-abhāva-saṃvedanād adhyātmam //

body.text: ahetur iti varttate / śarīre śarīre jñānavikalpānāṃ bhāvābhāvau saṃvedanīyau / asti me saṃśayajñānaṃ nāsti me saṃśayajñānam iti / evaṃ pratyakṣānumānāgamasmṛtijñāneṣu / seyam āvaraṇādyanupalabdhir upalabdhyabhāvaḥ svasaṃvedyaḥ -- nāsti me śabdasyāvaraṇādyupalabdhir iti nopalabdhyante śabdasyāgrahaṇakāraṇāny āvaraṇādīnīti / tatra yad uktaṃ tadanupalabdher anupalambhād abhāvasiddhir iti, etan nopapadyate //
body.translated_text: 'Without a valid reason' — this continues [from above]. In each body, the presence and absence of varieties of cognition are to be directly experienced: 'I have doubtful knowledge,' 'I do not have doubtful knowledge' — and similarly for cognitions of perception, inference, testimony, and memory. This non-perception of concealment and the like — the absence of apprehension — is self-evident: 'I do not have an apprehension of concealment, etc., of sound' — therefore the causes of non-apprehension of sound, such as concealment and the like, are not apprehended. Therefore, what was stated — 'from the non-perception of those [causes], non-existence is established through non-apprehension' — this is untenable.

children.text: ahetur iti varttate / śarīre śarīre jñāna-vikalpānāṃ bhāva-abhāvau saṃvedanīyau / asti me saṃśayajñānaṃ na asti me saṃśayajñānam iti / evaṃ pratyakṣa-anumāna-āgama-smṛti-jñāneṣu / sa īyam āvaraṇa-ādy-anupalabdhir upalabdhy-abhāvaḥ svasaṃvedyaḥ --- na asti me śabdasyā avaraṇa-ādy-upalabdhir iti na upalabdhyante śabdasya agrahaṇa-kāraṇāny āvaraṇa-ādīni iti / tatra yad uktaṃ tad-anupalabdher anupalambhād abhāva-siddhir iti, etan na upapadyate //

body.text: sādharmyāt tulyadharmopapatteḥ sarvānityatvaprasaṅgād anityasamaḥ // NySBh_5.1.32 sādharmyāt tulyadharmopapatteḥ sarvānityatvaprasaṅgād anityasamaḥ //5,1.32 anityena ghaṭena sādharmyād anityaḥ śabda iti bruvato 'sti ghaṭenānityena sarvabhāvānāṃ sādharmyam iti sarvasyānityatvam aniṣṭaṃ sampadyate / so 'yam anityatvena pratyavasthānād anityasama iti // NySBh_
body.translated_text: [The fallacy called] <s>anityasamaḥ</s> (the balancing of impermanence): because of similarity with what is impermanent, the establishment of a similar property, and the consequence that everything would be impermanent. When one says 'sound is impermanent because of its similarity with the impermanent pot,' there is similarity of all entities with the impermanent pot, and so the undesired consequence follows that everything is impermanent. This counter-objection through [universal] impermanence is [the fallacy called] <s>anityasamaḥ</s> (the balancing of impermanence).

children.text: sādharmyāt tulya-dharma upapatteḥ sarva-anityatva-prasaṅgād anityasamaḥ // NySBh_5.1.32 sādharmyāt tulya-dharma upapatteḥ sarva-anityatva-prasaṅgād anityasamaḥ //5,1.32 anityena ghaṭena sādharmyād anityaḥ śabda iti bruvato 'sti ghaṭena anityena sarvabhāvānāṃ sādharmyam iti sarvasya anityatvam aniṣṭaṃ sampadyate / so 'yam anityatvena pratyavasthānād anityasama iti // NySBh_

body.text: asyottaram
body.translated_text: The answer to this:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: sādharmyād asiddheḥ pratiṣedhāsiddhiḥ pratiṣedhyasādharmyāt //
body.translated_text: Because of the non-establishment [of the thesis] through [mere] similarity, the non-establishment of the refutation [follows] from its similarity with what is to be refuted.

children.text: sādharmyād asiddheḥ pratiṣedha-asiddhiḥ pratiṣedhya-sādharmyāt //

body.text: pratijñādyavayavayuktaṃ vākyaṃ pakṣanivartakaṃ pratipakṣalakṣaṇaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ / tasya pakṣeṇa pratiṣedhyena sādharmyaṃ pratijñādiyogaḥ / tad yady anityasādharmyād anityatvasyāsiddhiḥ, sādharmyād asiddheḥ pratiṣedhasyāpy asiddhiḥ, pratiṣedhyena sādharmyād iti //
body.translated_text: A refutation (<s>pratiṣedha</s>) is a statement equipped with the components of thesis and the rest that overturns the opponent's position. Its similarity with the thesis being refuted consists in possessing the components of thesis and the rest. If, then, impermanence is not established through mere similarity with what is impermanent, then by the same token, the refutation too is not established through its similarity with what is to be refuted, since [it too shares mere] similarity.

children.text: pratijñā-ādy-avayava-yuktaṃ vākyaṃ pakṣa-nivartakaṃ pratipakṣa-lakṣaṇaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ / tasya pakṣeṇa pratiṣedhyena sādharmyaṃ pratijñā-ādi-yogaḥ / tad yady anitya-sādharmyād anityatvasya asiddhiḥ, sādharmyād asiddheḥ pratiṣedhasya apy asiddhiḥ, pratiṣedhyena sādharmyād iti //

body.text: dṛṣṭānte ca sādhyasādhanabhāvena prajñātasya dharmasya hetutvāt tasya cobhayathābhāvān nāviśeṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: And because the property recognized in the example as having the relation of probandum and probans is the reason, and because that [property] has both [aspects], there is no non-distinction.

children.text: dṛṣṭānte ca sādhya-sādhana-bhāvena prajñātasya dharmasya hetutvāt tasya ca ubhayathā-bhāvān na aviśeṣaḥ //

body.text: dṛṣṭānte yaḥ khalu dharmaḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvena prajñāyate, sa hetutvenābhidhīyate / sa cobhayathā bhavati, kenacit samānaḥ kutaścid viśiṣṭaḥ / sāmānyāt sādharmyaṃ viśeṣāc ca vaidharmyam / evaṃ sādharmyaviśeṣo hetuḥ, nāviśeṣeṇa sādharmyamātraṃ vaidharmyamātraṃ vā / sādharmyamātraṃ vaidharmyamātraṃ cāśritya bhavān āha --"sādharmyāt tulyadharmopapatteḥ sarvānityatvaprasaṅgād anityasama" iti, etad ayuktam iti / aviśeṣasamapratiṣedhe ca yad uktaṃ tad api veditavyam //
body.translated_text: The property that is recognized in the example as having the relation of probandum and probans — that is declared to be the reason. And that [property] has both aspects: in some respect it is similar [to the subject], and in some respect it is different. From the common aspect comes similarity; from the distinctive aspect comes dissimilarity. Thus the reason consists of both similarity and distinction, not merely undifferentiated similarity alone or dissimilarity alone. Having resorted to mere similarity or mere dissimilarity, you say 'the balancing of impermanence because of similarity and the consequence of universal impermanence' — this is unjustified. And what was stated in the refutation of <s>aviśeṣasama</s> (the balancing of non-distinction) should also be understood here.

children.text: dṛṣṭānte yaḥ khalu dharmaḥ sādhya-sādhana-bhāvena prajñāyate, sa hetutvena abhidhīyate / sa ca ubhayathā bhavati, kenacit samānaḥ kutaścid viśiṣṭaḥ / sāmānyāt sādharmyaṃ viśeṣāc ca vaidharmyam / evaṃ sādharmya-viśeṣo hetuḥ, na aviśeṣeṇa sādharmya-mātraṃ vaidharmya-mātraṃ vā / sādharmya-mātraṃ vaidharmya-mātraṃ cā aśritya bhavān āha ---"sādharmyāt tulya-dharma-upapatteḥ sarva-anityatva-prasaṅgād anityasama" iti, etad ayuktam iti / aviśeṣasama-pratiṣedhe ca yad uktaṃ tad api veditavyam //

body.text: nityam anityabhāvād anitye nityatvopapatter nityasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: [The fallacy called] <s>nityasamaḥ</s> (the balancing of eternality): because the impermanent nature is either eternal or impermanent in what is impermanent.

children.text: nityam anitya-bhāvād anitye nityatva-upapatter nityasamaḥ //

body.text: anityaḥ śabda iti pratijñāyate / tad anityatvaṃ kiṃ śabde nityam athānityam ? yadi tāvat sarvadā bhavati ? dharmasya sadā bhāvād dharmiṇo 'pi sadā bhāva iti nityaḥ śabda iti / atha na sarvadā bhavati ? anityatvasyābhāvān nityaḥ śabdaḥ / evaṃ nityatvena pratyavasthānān nityasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: It is asserted that 'sound is impermanent.' Is that impermanence eternal or impermanent in sound? If it exists at all times — then from the permanent presence of the property, the permanent existence of the property-bearer [follows], hence sound is eternal. If it does not exist at all times — then from the absence of impermanence, sound is eternal. Thus, the counter-objection through eternality is [the fallacy called] <s>nityasamaḥ</s> (the balancing of eternality).

children.text: anityaḥ śabda iti pratijñāyate / tad anityatvaṃ kiṃ śabde nityam atha anityam ? yadi tāvat sarvadā bhavati ? dharmasya sadā bhāvād dharmiṇo 'pi sadā bhāva iti nityaḥ śabda iti / atha na sarvadā bhavati ? anityatvasya abhāvān nityaḥ śabdaḥ / evaṃ nityatvena pratyavasthānān nityasamaḥ //

body.text: asyottaram
body.translated_text: The answer to this:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: pratiṣedhye nityam anityabhāvād anitye 'nityatvopapatteḥ pratiṣedhābhāvaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because impermanence is permanently [present] in what is to be refuted, and because in what is impermanent, impermanence is established, the refutation fails.

children.text: pratiṣedhye nityam anitya-bhāvād anitye 'nityatva-upapatteḥ pratiṣedha-abhāvaḥ //

body.text: pratiṣedhye śabde nityam anityatvasya bhāvād ity ucyamāne 'nujñātaṃ śabdasyānityatvam, anityatvopapatteś ca "nānityaḥ śabda" iti pratiṣedho nopapadyate / atha nābhyupagamyate, nityam anityatvasya bhāvād iti hetur na bhavatīti hetvabhāvāt pratiṣedhānupapattir iti / utapannasya nirodhād abhāvaḥ śabdasyānityatvaṃ, tatra paripraśnānupapattiḥ / yo 'yaṃ paripaśnaḥ -- tad anityatvaṃ kiṃ śabde sarvadā bhavati atha neti, ayam anupapannaḥ / kasmāt ? utpannasya yo nirodhād abhāvaḥ śabdasya tad anityatvam ; evaṃ ca saty adhikaraṇādheyavibhāgo vyāghātān nāstīti / nityānityatvavirodhāc ca / nityatvam anityatvaṃ ca ekasya dharmiṇo dharmāv iti virudhyete, na sambhavataḥ / tatra yad uktaṃ -- nityam anityatvasya bhāvān nitya eva, tad avartamānārtham uktam iti //
body.translated_text: When it is said 'because non-eternality always exists in what is to be negated, namely sound' — the non-eternality of sound is thereby conceded; and since non-eternality is logically established, the negation 'sound is not non-eternal' is not logically possible. But if [the opponent says] that is not admitted, then the reason 'because non-eternality always exists' does not hold — and from the absence of the reason, the negation is not established. [Consider:] the non-eternality of sound is the non-existence [of sound] through the cessation of what has arisen. In that case, the cross-question is not valid. The cross-question 'Does that non-eternality always exist in sound, or not?' — this is invalid. Why? Because the non-eternality of sound is the non-existence [of sound] through the cessation of what has arisen; and this being so, the distinction between substratum and superimposed property does not exist, due to contradiction. And because of the contradiction between eternality and non-eternality — eternality and non-eternality, being properties of one and the same subject (<s>dharmin</s>), are contradictory and cannot co-exist. Therefore, what was stated — 'because non-eternality always exists, [sound] is indeed eternal' — is stated with a meaning that does not obtain.

children.text: pratiṣedhye śabde nityam anityatvasya bhāvād ity ucyamāne 'nujñātaṃ śabdasya anityatvam, anityatva-upapatteś ca "na anityaḥ śabda" iti pratiṣedho na upapadyate / atha na abhyupagamyate, nityam anityatvasya bhāvād iti hetur na bhavati iti hetv-abhāvāt pratiṣedha-anupapattir iti / utapannasya nirodhād abhāvaḥ śabdasya anityatvaṃ, tatra paripraśna-anupapattiḥ / yo 'yaṃ paripaśnaḥ --- tad anityatvaṃ kiṃ śabde sarvadā bhavati atha na iti, ayam anupapannaḥ / kasmāt ? utpannasya yo nirodhād abhāvaḥ śabdasya tad anityatvam ; evaṃ ca saty adhikaraṇa-ādheya-vibhāgo vyāghātān na asti iti / nitya-anityatva-virodhāc ca / nityatvam anityatvaṃ ca ekasya dharmiṇo dharmāv iti virudhyete, na sambhavataḥ / tatra yad uktaṃ --- nityam anityatvasya bhāvān nitya eva, tad avartamāna-artham uktam iti //

body.text: prayatnakāryānekatvāt kāryasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Because of the multiplicity of effects of effort, [there is] the fallacy of being equal to the effect (<s>kāryasama</s>). ||

children.text: prayatna-kārya-anekatvāt kāryasamaḥ //

body.text: prayatnānantarīyakatvād anityaḥ śabda iti / yasya prayatnānantaram ātmalābhaḥ tat khalv abhūtvā bhavati, yathā ghaṭādikāryam ; anityam iti ca bhūtvā na bhavatīty etad vijñāyate / evam avasthite prayatnakāryānekatvād iti pratiṣedha ucyate / prayatnānantaram ātmalābhaś ca dṛṣṭo ghaṭādīnām, vyavadhānāpohāc cābhivyaktir vyavahitānām / tat kiṃ prayatnānantaram ātmalābhaḥ śabdasyāho 'bhivyaktir iti viśeṣo nāsti / kāryāviśeṣeṇa pratyavasthānaṃ kāryasamaḥ //
body.translated_text: Sound is non-eternal because it arises immediately after effort. That which comes into existence immediately after effort — that indeed, not having existed before, comes into being, like effects such as a pot; and what is known as 'non-eternal' means that, having existed, it ceases to exist. This being the case, the negation is stated: 'because of the multiplicity of effects of effort.' The coming into existence immediately after effort is observed in pots and the like, while [in the case of things previously existing but hidden,] manifestation [occurs] through the removal of obstruction for things that were obscured. So, whether there is coming-into-existence immediately after effort for sound, or manifestation — there is no distinction. The counterbalancing through the non-distinction of the effect is [the fallacy called] <s>kāryasama</s> (equal to the effect).

children.text: prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād anityaḥ śabda iti / yasya prayatna-anantaram ātma-lābhaḥ tat khalv abhūtvā bhavati, yathā ghaṭa-ādi-kāryam ; anityam iti ca bhūtvā na bhavati ity etad vijñāyate / evam avasthite prayatna-kārya-anekatvād iti pratiṣedha ucyate / prayatna-anantaram ātma-lābhaś ca dṛṣṭo ghaṭa-ādīnām, vyavadhāna-apohāc ca abhivyaktir vyavahitānām / tat kiṃ prayatna-anantaram ātma-lābhaḥ śabdasya aho 'bhivyaktir iti viśeṣo na asti / kārya-aviśeṣeṇa pratyavasthānaṃ kāryasamaḥ //

body.text: asyottaram
body.translated_text: The reply to this [is as follows]:

children.text: asya uttaram

body.text: kāryānyatve prayatnāhetutvam anupalabdhikāraṇopapatteḥ //
body.translated_text: If the effect is different [from mere manifestation], effort is not the cause, because the cause of non-perception is logically explained. ||

children.text: kārya-anyatve prayatna-ahetutvam anupalabdhi-kāraṇa-upapatteḥ //

body.text: sati kāryānyatve anupalabdhikāraṇopapatteḥ prayatnasyāhetutvaṃ śabdasyābhivyaktau / yatra prayatnānantaram abhivyaktis tatrānupalabdhikāraṇaṃ vyavadhānam upapadyate, vyavadhānāpohāc ca prayatnānantarabhāvino 'rthasyopalabdhilakṣaṇābhivyaktir bhavatīti, na tu śabdasyānupalabdhikāraṇaṃ kiṃcid upapadyate, yasya prayatnānantaram apohāc chabdasyopalabhilakṣaṇābhivyaktir bhavatīti, tasmād utpadyate śabdo nābhivyajyate iti //
body.translated_text: Given that the effect is different [i.e., that sound is produced, not merely manifested], effort is not the cause of the manifestation of sound, because the cause of non-perception is logically explained. Where manifestation occurs immediately after effort, there obstruction, which is the cause of non-perception, is logically established, and from the removal of obstruction, there is manifestation — defined as perception — of the object that comes into being immediately after [the removal]. But no cause of non-perception of sound is logically possible, by the removal of which there would be manifestation — defined as perception — of sound. Therefore, sound is produced, not manifested.

children.text: sati kārya-anyatve anupalabdhi-kāraṇa-upapatteḥ prayatnasya ahetutvaṃ śabdasya abhivyaktau / yatra prayatna-anantaram abhivyaktis tatra anupalabdhi-kāraṇaṃ vyavadhānam upapadyate, vyavadhāna-apohāc ca prayatna-anantara-bhāvino 'rthasya upalabdhilakṣaṇa ābhivyaktir bhavati iti, na tu śabdasya anupalabdhi-kāraṇaṃ kiṃcid upapadyate, yasya prayatna-anantaram apohāc chabdasya upalabhi-lakṣaṇa ābhivyaktir bhavati iti, tasmād utpadyate śabdo na abhivyajyate iti //

body.text: hetoś ced anaikāntikatvam upapadyate anaikātikatvād asādhakaḥ syād iti / yadi cānaikāntikatvād asādhakatvam --
body.translated_text: If the reason [offered] has the character of being inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>), then, being inconclusive, it would not be probative. And if [it is argued that] being non-probative [follows] from inconclusiveness —

children.text: hetoś ced anaikāntikatvam upapadyate anaikātikatvād asādhakaḥ syād iti / yadi ca anaikāntikatvād asādhakatvam ---

body.text: pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the negation too, the same fault [applies]. ||

children.text: pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣaḥ //

body.text: pratiṣedho 'py anaikāntikaḥ, kiṃcit pratiṣedhati kiṃcin neti anaikāntikatvād asādhaka iti / atha vā śabdasyānityatvapakṣe prayatnānantaram utpādo nābhivyaktir iti viśeṣahetvabhāvaḥ, nityatvapakṣe 'pi prayatnānantaram abhivyaktir notpāda iti viśeṣahetvabhāvaḥ / so 'yam ubhayapakṣasamo viśeṣahetvabhāva ity ubhayam apy anaikātikam iti //
body.translated_text: The negation too is inconclusive — it negates some [instances] and not others — and being inconclusive, it is non-probative.
