Or alternatively: in the thesis of the non-eternality of sound, there is an absence of a distinguishing reason [to show that] what follows effort is origination and not manifestation; in the thesis of eternality too, there is an absence of a distinguishing reason [to show that] what follows effort is manifestation and not origination. This absence of a distinguishing reason is equal on both sides — therefore both are inconclusive.

children.text: pratiṣedho 'py anaikāntikaḥ, kiṃcit pratiṣedhati kiṃcin na iti anaikāntikatvād asādhaka iti / atha vā śabdasya anityatva-pakṣe prayatna-anantaram utpādo na abhivyaktir iti viśeṣa-hetv-abhāvaḥ, nityatva-pakṣe 'pi prayatna-anantaram abhivyaktir na utpāda iti viśeṣa-hetv-abhāvaḥ / so 'yam ubhaya-pakṣa-samo viśeṣa-hetv-abhāva ity ubhayam apy anaikātikam iti //

body.text: sarvatraivam //
body.translated_text: In all cases, the same [applies]. ||

children.text: sarvatra evam //

body.text: sarveṣu sādharmyaprabhṛtiṣu pratiṣedhahetuṣu yatra yatrāviśeṣo dṛśyate tatrobhayoḥ pakṣayoḥ samaḥ prasajyata iti //
body.translated_text: In all [fallacious] counter-reasons beginning with <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) and so on, wherever a lack of distinction is seen, the same [fault] applies equally to both positions.

children.text: sarveṣu sādharmya-prabhṛtiṣu pratiṣedha-hetuṣu yatra yatra aviśeṣo dṛśyate tatra ubhayoḥ pakṣayoḥ samaḥ prasajyata iti //

body.text: pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe pratiṣedhadoṣavad doṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: In the counter-negation of the negation, the fault is the same as the fault of the negation. ||

children.text: pratiṣedha-vipratiṣedhe pratiṣedha-doṣavad doṣaḥ //

body.text: yo 'yaṃ pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣo 'naikāntikatvam āpadyate so 'yaṃ pratiṣedhasya vipratiṣedhe 'pi samānaḥ / tatrānityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād iti sādhanavādinaḥ sthāpanā prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ / "prayatnakāryānekatvāt kāryasama" iti dūṣaṇavādinaḥ pratiṣedhahetunā dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ / sa ca pratiṣedha ity ucyate / tasyāsya pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa iti tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ vipratiṣedha ucyate / tasmin pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣo 'naikāntikatvaṃ caturthaḥ pakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: This fault of inconclusiveness that arises even in the negation — that same [fault] applies also in the counter-negation of the negation. There, 'Sound is non-eternal because it arises immediately after effort' is the establishment by the proponent — the first thesis. 'Because of the multiplicity of effects of effort, [there is the fallacy] equal to the effect' — through the counter-reason of the objector — is the second thesis, and that is called the negation. 'Even in the negation, the same fault [applies]' — is the third thesis, called the counter-negation. In that counter-negation of the negation, too, the same fault of inconclusiveness — is the fourth thesis.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣo 'naikāntikatvam āpadyate so 'yaṃ pratiṣedhasya vipratiṣedhe 'pi samānaḥ / tatra anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatna-ānantarīyakatvād iti sādhana-vādinaḥ sthāpanā prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ / "prayatna-kārya-anekatvāt kāryasama" iti dūṣaṇa-vādinaḥ pratiṣedha-hetunā dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ / sa ca pratiṣedha ity ucyate / tasya asya pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa iti tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ vipratiṣedha ucyate / tasmin pratiṣedha-vipratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣo 'naikāntikatvaṃ caturthaḥ pakṣaḥ //

body.text: pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣam abhyupetya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe samāno doṣaprasaṅgo matānujñā //
body.translated_text: Having accepted the negation as faulty, [yet still] pressing the same fault in the counter-negation of the negation constitutes the fault of conceding the [opponent's] position (<s>matānujñā</s>). ||

children.text: pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣam abhyupetya pratiṣedha-vipratiṣedhe samāno doṣa-prasaṅgo mata-anujñā //

body.text: pratiṣedhaṃ dvitīyaṃ pakṣaṃ sadoṣam abhyupetya taduddhāram akṛtvānujñāya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe tṛtīyapakṣe samānam anaikāntikatvam iti samānaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ prasañjayato dūṣaṇavādino matānujñā prasajyata iti pañcamaḥ pakṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: Having accepted the negation (the second thesis) as faulty, without removing that [fault], having conceded it, and then pressing the same inconclusiveness as an equal fault in the counter-negation (the third thesis) — for the objector who presses the same fault, the fault of conceding the [opponent's] position (<s>matānujñā</s>) arises — this is the fifth thesis.

children.text: pratiṣedhaṃ dvitīyaṃ pakṣaṃ sadoṣam abhyupetya tad-uddhāram akṛtva ānujñāya pratiṣedha-vipratiṣedhe tṛtīya-pakṣe samānam anaikāntikatvam iti samānaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ prasañjayato dūṣaṇa-vādino mata-anujñā prasajyata iti pañcamaḥ pakṣaḥ //

body.text: svapakṣalakṣaṇāpekṣopapattyupasaṃhāre hetunirdeśe parapakṣadoṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣaḥ //
body.translated_text: When, relying on the fault characteristic of one's own thesis, one draws a conclusion and states the reason, from the acceptance of the fault in the opponent's thesis, the same fault [applies]. ||

children.text: sva-pakṣa-lakṣaṇa-apekṣā-upapatty-upasaṃhāre hetu-nirdeśe para-pakṣa-doṣa-abhyupagamāt samāno doṣaḥ //

body.text: sthāpanāpakṣe prayatnakāryānekatvād iti doṣaḥ sthāpanāhetuvādinaḥ svapakṣalakṣaṇo bhavati / kasmāt ? svapakṣasamutthatvāt / so 'yaṃ svapakṣalakṣaṇaṃ doṣam apekṣamāṇo 'nuddhṛtyānujñāya pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa ity upapadyamānaṃ doṣaṃ parapakṣe upasaṃharati / itthaṃ cānaikāntikaḥ pratiṣedha iti hetuṃ nirdiśati / tatra svapakṣalakṣaṇāpekṣayopapadyamānadoṣopasaṃhāre hetunirdeśe ca saty anena parapakṣadoṣo 'bhyupagato bhavati / kathaṃ kṛtvā ? yaḥ pareṇa prayatnakāryānekatvādityādinānaikāntikadoṣa uktaḥ, tam anuddhṛtya pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa ity āha / evaṃ sthāpanāṃ sadoṣām abhyupetya pratiṣedhe 'pi samānaṃ doṣaṃ prasañjayataḥ parapakṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣo bhavati / yathā parasya pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣam abhyupetya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣaprasaṅgo matānujñā prasajyata iti, tathāsyāpi sthāpanāṃ sadoṣām abhyupetya pratiṣedhe 'pi samānaṃ doṣaṃ prasañjayato matānujñā prasajyata iti / sa khalv ayaṃ ṣaṣṭaḥ pakṣaḥ / tatra khalu sthāpanāhetuvādinaḥ prathamatṛtīyapañcamapakṣāḥ, pratiṣedhahetuvādinaḥ dvitīyacaturthaṣaṣṭapakṣāḥ teṣāṃ sādhvasādhutāyāṃ mīmāṃsyamānāyāṃ caturthaṣaṣṭayor arthāviśeṣāt punaruktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ / caturthapakṣe samānadoṣatvaṃ parasyocyate --"pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe pratiṣedhadoṣavad doṣa" iti / ṣaṣṭe 'pi "parapakṣadoṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣa" iti samānadoṣatvam evocyate, nārthaviśeṣaḥ kaścid asti / samānas tṛṭīyapañcamayoḥ punaruktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ, tṛṭīyapakṣe 'pi "pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa" iti samānatvam abhyupagamyate / pañcamapakṣe 'pi "pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe samāno doṣaprasaṅgo"+abhyupagamyate, nārthaviśeṣaḥ kaścid ucyata iti / tatra pañcamaṣaṣṭapakṣayor arthāviśeṣāt punaruktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ, tṛtīyacaturthayor matānujñā, prathamadvitīyayor viśeṣahetvabhāva iti ṣaṭpakṣyām ubhayor asiddhiḥ / kadā ṣaṭpakṣī ? yadā "pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa" ity evaṃ pravarttate / tadobhayoḥ pakṣayor asiddhiḥ / yadā tu "kāryānyatve prayatnāhetutvam anupalabdhikāraṇopapatter" ity anena tṛṭīyapakṣo yajyate, tadā viśeṣahetuvacanāt "prayatnānantaram ātmalābhaḥ śabdasya, nābhivyaktir" iti siddhaḥ prathamapakṣo na ṣaṭpakṣī pravartata iti //
body.translated_text: In the establishment thesis, the fault 'because of the multiplicity of effects of effort' belongs to the proponent's own thesis. Why? Because it arises from his own thesis. This [proponent], relying on this fault characteristic of his own thesis, without removing it, having conceded it, draws a conclusion that 'even in the negation, the same fault [applies]' and attributes the arising fault to the opponent's thesis. In this way, 'the negation is inconclusive' — thus he states the reason. In that case, when, relying on a fault characteristic of one's own thesis, one draws a conclusion regarding an arising fault and states a reason — by this, the fault in the opponent's thesis is accepted [as applying to one's own]. How so? The fault of inconclusiveness stated by the opponent through 'because of the multiplicity of effects of effort' and so on — without removing that, he says 'even in the negation, the same fault applies.' Thus, having accepted the establishment as faulty, for one who presses the same fault even in the negation, the same fault arises from accepting the opponent's thesis. Just as, for the opponent, having accepted the negation as faulty and pressing the same fault in the counter-negation, the fault of conceding the position arises — so too for this one, having accepted the establishment as faulty and pressing the same fault in the negation, the fault of conceding the position arises. This indeed is the sixth thesis. In that [scheme], the proponent holds the first, third, and fifth theses, while the objector holds the second, fourth, and sixth theses. When their validity is examined, between the fourth and sixth theses there is no distinction of meaning — [hence] the fault of redundancy arises. In the fourth thesis, it is stated that 'the same fault applies to the opponent' — 'in the counter-negation of the negation, the fault is the same as the fault of the negation.' In the sixth too, 'from the acceptance of the fault in the opponent's thesis, the same fault [applies]' — the very same equality of fault is stated, without any distinction of meaning. The same fault of redundancy arises between the third and fifth theses. In the third thesis too, 'even in the negation, the same fault [applies]' — equality is accepted. In the fifth thesis too, 'in the counter-negation of the negation, the same fault arises' — is accepted, without any distinction of meaning being stated. Therefore, between the fifth and sixth theses there is the fault of redundancy; between the third and fourth, there is the conceding of position (<s>matānujñā</s>); between the first and second, there is the absence of a distinguishing reason — thus in the six-thesis scheme, neither side is established. When does the six-thesis scheme arise? When one proceeds [to say] 'even in the negation, the same fault [applies].' Then neither thesis is established. But when, through the third thesis 'if the effect is different, effort is not the cause, because the cause of non-perception is logically explained,' a distinguishing reason is stated — [namely] that 'the coming-into-existence immediately after effort belongs to sound, not manifestation' — then the first thesis is established and the six-thesis scheme does not arise.

children.text: sthāpanā-pakṣe prayatna-kārya-anekatvād iti doṣaḥ sthāpanā-hetu-vādinaḥ sva-pakṣa-lakṣaṇo bhavati / kasmāt ? sva-pakṣa-samutthatvāt / so 'yaṃ sva-pakṣa-lakṣaṇaṃ doṣam apekṣamāṇo 'nuddhṛtya anujñāya pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa ity upapadyamānaṃ doṣaṃ para-pakṣe upasaṃharati / itthaṃ ca anaikāntikaḥ pratiṣedha iti hetuṃ nirdiśati / tatra sva-pakṣa-lakṣaṇa-apekṣaya ūpapadyamāna-doṣa-upasaṃhāre hetu-nirdeśe ca saty anena para-pakṣa-doṣo 'bhyupagato bhavati / kathaṃ kṛtvā ? yaḥ pareṇa prayatna-kārya-anekatvād-ity-ādina ānaikāntika-doṣa uktaḥ, tam anuddhṛtya pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa ity āha / evaṃ sthāpanāṃ sadoṣām abhyupetya pratiṣedhe 'pi samānaṃ doṣaṃ prasañjayataḥ para-pakṣa-abhyupagamāt samāno doṣo bhavati / yathā parasya pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣam abhyupetya pratiṣedha-vipratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣaprasaṅgo mata-anujñā prasajyata iti, tatha āsya api sthāpanāṃ sadoṣām abhyupetya pratiṣedhe 'pi samānaṃ doṣaṃ prasañjayato mata-anujñā prasajyata iti / sa khalv ayaṃ ṣaṣṭaḥ pakṣaḥ / tatra khalu sthāpanā-hetu-vādinaḥ prathama-tṛtīya-pañcama-pakṣāḥ, pratiṣedha-hetu-vādinaḥ dvitīya-caturtha-ṣaṣṭa-pakṣāḥ teṣāṃ sādhv-asādhutāyāṃ mīmāṃsyamānāyāṃ caturtha-ṣaṣṭayor artha-aviśeṣāt punar-ukta-doṣa-prasaṅgaḥ / caturtha-pakṣe samāna-doṣatvaṃ parasya ucyate ---"pratiṣedha-vipratiṣedhe pratiṣedha-doṣavad doṣa" iti / ṣaṣṭe 'pi "para-pakṣa-doṣa-abhyupagamāt samāno doṣa" iti samāna-doṣatvam eva ucyate, na artha-viśeṣaḥ kaścid asti / samānas tṛṭīya-pañcamayoḥ punar-ukta-doṣa-prasaṅgaḥ, tṛṭīya-pakṣe 'pi "pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa" iti samānatvam abhyupagamyate / pañcama-pakṣe 'pi "pratiṣedha-vipratiṣedhe samāno doṣa-prasaṅgo"+abhyupagamyate, na artha-viśeṣaḥ kaścid ucyata iti / tatra pañcama-ṣaṣṭa-pakṣayor artha-aviśeṣāt punar-ukta-doṣa-prasaṅgaḥ, tṛtīya-caturthayor mata-anujñā, prathama-dvitīyayor viśeṣa-hetv-abhāva iti ṣaṭpakṣyām ubhayor asiddhiḥ / kadā ṣaṭpakṣī ? yadā "pratiṣedhe 'pi samāno doṣa" ity evaṃ pravarttate / tada ūbhayoḥ pakṣayor asiddhiḥ / yadā tu "kārya-anyatve prayatna-ahetutvam anupalabdhi-kāraṇa-upapatter" ity anena tṛṭīya-pakṣo yajyate, tadā viśeṣa-hetu-vacanāt "prayatna-anantaram ātma-lābhaḥ śabdasya, na abhivyaktir" iti siddhaḥ prathama-pakṣo na ṣaṭpakṣī pravartata iti //
